# Preface

## To the Art-Desiring
## Reader.

I must indeed myself confess that already a considerable number of chemical <note>The original "Chymischer" refers to the early modern period when chemistry and alchemy were not yet distinct sciences.</note> books are available, for which reason I should rightly hesitate to fill the world with even more of them.

However, because these excellent writings of **MICHAEL SENDIVOGIUS** <note>original: "MICHAELIS SENDIVOGII." Sendivogius was a famous Polish alchemist and physician (1566–1636), renowned for his theories on the "food of life" in the air.</note> have been lacking for a considerable time, yet have nevertheless been so eagerly sought by many, I have wished to remedy this lack through this new edition.

As far as I am aware, this jewel in the German language has not been printed more than three times, namely in the year 1613, 1628, and the year 1681, in octavo <term>octavo (8vo): a printing format where a large sheet of paper is folded three times to create eight leaves, resulting in a portable, medium-sized book.</term> in Strasbourg.

<summary>In this preface, the publisher justifies printing a new edition of the alchemist Michael Sendivogius's works, noting that while many chemical books exist, these specific writings are rare and in high demand.</summary>

# To the Reader.

The author of the *New Chemical Light* <note>original Latin: *Novi Luminis Chemici*</note> is either **SETHON**, a **SCOT**, whom the Germans call **SIDONIUS**; it does not matter much <note>original Latin: *non multum refert*</note> (among the classic writers of this Art <term>Art: In this context, "The Art" refers to Alchemy</term> he is usually numbered by everyone’s judgment thus far). He is a candid author (as much as the "religion" of the Philosophers <term>Philosophers: A term used by alchemists to refer to themselves as seekers of natural wisdom</term> permits) and opens his meaning without the fabrications of chemical processes and without inverted or slippery words. In his parables, he is even more free and closer to the truth. But, lest we conceal anything, he is crafty within that image of candor, turning his pen one way and his mind another; so much so that those who follow him too closely according to the literal word can easily be led astray. His *Dialogue between Mercury and the Alchemist* charms with its wit and jokes, but in the "principal knot" <note>The central mystery or most difficult part of the alchemical operation.</note> it does not explain itself sufficiently. There also exists a *Treatise* of **SENDIVOGIUS** *concerning the Sulfur of the Philosophers*; it is not written carelessly, yet, as is clear from certain signs, it is by no means to be attributed to **SENDIVOGIUS**.

he himself <note>Referring to Alexander Seton on his deathbed</note> handed over to his friend **SENDIVOGIUS** his wife, his transmutation powder <term>Transmutation powder: Also known as the "Projection Powder," this was the physical form of the Philosopher's Stone used to transform base metals into gold</term>, and also the manuscript, which consists of twelve books. This governor imprisoned him so securely that **SENDIVOGIUS** could not escape, forcing him to give up a portion of the transmutation powder and to entrust him with the secret knowledge. **SENDIVOGIUS** did not possess the knowledge himself <note>That is, he possessed the powder given by Seton, but not the recipe to make more</note>, (d) but entrusted him with something false. ->To the Reader,<-

This bird <note>A disparaging idiomatic term for the district governor mentioned on the previous page</note> now boasted of the **Philosopher's Stone** <term>Philosopher's Stone: The legendary substance capable of turning base metals into gold, also called the "transmutation stone"</term> and made the **Duke** believe he had a master of the Art at his court. **SENDIVOGIUS** is forgotten, and the district governor knows how to artfully intercept the letters sent to him so that no one suspects him; finally, the work comes to an end, and the end is a heap of filth <note>A common alchemical expression for a failed experiment; the "Great Work" resulted in nothing but waste</note>. The district governor apologizes to the Prince but secretly torments the unknowing **SENDIVOGIUS**, who, regarding the matter which he does not understand <margin>(e)</margin>, devises a false process; however, **SENDIVOGIUS** seeks to escape at night with the help of bedsheets but breaks a leg in two, so he must return to his old quarters. Through this, the matter becomes somewhat known; **SENDIVOGIUS** was in prison for a year and a half, during which time the district governor intercepted and answered all the Royal Polish letters until he once made a mistake and allowed a letter to be received by the **Duke** without his knowledge. Then the matter was entirely betrayed, and a hypothetical case was presented to the official in which he himself judged that a "double gallows" <note>A severe form of execution for high-ranking officials or particularly heinous crimes</note> was the appropriate punishment—a sentence which, after an investigation, was carried out upon him. **SENDIVOGIUS**, however, went free, as the judicial letters testify. Thus **SENDIVOGIUS** has endured sufficient punishment for his presumption <margin>(f)</margin>.

Speaking of the book itself, it reveals various parts, such as first, the seven months and ten months <note>These likely refer to alchemical time cycles required for the "Great Work" of transmutation</note>. Secondly, Neptune and Saturn <note>In alchemy, Neptune often represents the solvent or "water," while Saturn represents lead or the "nigredo" (blackening) stage</note>; thirdly, the different furnace operations. ### Dr. Conrad Horlacher (g)

This man calls him the noble, the famous, the fundamentally learned, and profound adept <term>Adept: A master of the alchemical arts who has supposedly achieved the secret of the Philosopher's Stone</term>. He also consistently accepts him as the true author of these writings.

->To the Reader.<-

I could provide many more such judgments, regarding both his writings and his life; however, since it is not my intention at this time to describe the life of **SENDIVOGIUS** in great detail, may the kind reader be satisfied for now as I speak briefly:

**MICHAEL SENDIVOGIUS** was a Polish nobleman and was born in the year 1566 in the region of **SANDEZ**, which falls under the jurisdiction of the Krakow Voivodeship <note>A Voivodeship is a high-level administrative province in Poland, similar to a duchy or state</note>.

**JACOB SANDIMIRUS**, of whom **SENDIVOGIUS** was the natural son, had him raised with good morals and especially encouraged him to study diligently, for which **SENDIVOGIUS** showed a great desire from his youth. As he zealously continued his studies, among other books, the chemical writings of **ARNOLDUS de VILLA NOVA** <note>Arnold of Villanova (c. 1240–1311) was a famous medieval physician, alchemist, and religious reformer</note> came into his hands. Through these, he was encouraged to reflect further on this great mystery, after he had completed the necessary humanities studies <note>original: "studia in humanioribus"; this refers to the classical liberal arts education required of scholars</note> and laid the foundation for the greater edifice of learning.

### The Third Labor.
#### Concerning the Fixed Salt.

The residual earth remaining in the bottom of the retort from the distillation should be calcined <note>Calcination is the process of heating a substance to high temperatures in the presence of air to remove impurities or change its chemical state.</note> in an open fire for 12 hours, until it is reduced to ashes; let lukewarm distilled rainwater be poured over it, and the fixed salt <note>original: "sal fixum"</note> will be extracted into the water. Filter the extraction, which is removed by decanting <note>original: "per inclinationem" — the process of tilting a vessel to pour off liquid while leaving sediment behind.</note>: pour on fresh hot water until no saltiness remains to be extracted from the earth; you will observe and recognize this if the poured water remains sweet <note>meaning tasteless or non-salty.</note>. This earth which remains is called the cursed and condemned earth <note>original: "terra maledicta, & damnata"</note>; discard this, for it is of no use in the work. Filter all the extractions and coagulate them until they become crystalline and very pure. And thus, the third labor is also completed.

### Preparation of saltpeter from a second virgin earth <note>Virgin earth refers to soil that has not been depleted or previously used for extraction, believed to contain "astral" salts.</note>.

# A Secret of All Secrets, from Mr. Johann Joachim Becher’s *Chemical Port of Fortune*. <note>original: "Chymischen Glücks Hafen"</note> p. 218.

Take [℞] calcined **Gold** <term>Gold: Represented by the symbol ☉ (Sol). Calcined gold is gold that has been reduced to a fine powder through intense heat.</term>, lay it on a cupel <note>A shallow, porous dish used in assaying and refining precious metals.</note>, place it in a reverberatory furnace <note>A furnace that reflects heat from the roof onto the material being heated.</note>, and reverberate it until you see beautiful flowers <note>original: "flores"; in alchemy, these are the sublimated vapors that crystallize on the surface.</note> appearing on the lime. When that has happened, take the lime along with the flowers and throw them into our **Spirit** <term>Spirit: Marked by the symbol ⚹, which usually denotes Sal Ammoniac, but here explicitly identified by the author as Spirit of Wine (alcohol).</term>, that is, in Spirit of Wine <note>original: "S.V." (Spiritus Vini)</note>. Thus the flowers dissolve in the **Spirit** [⚹]. Once they have dissolved, pour the **Spirit** [⚹] very gently away from the lime, dry it, and reverberate it again until flowers appear. Pour it back into our **Spirit** [⚹], and do this for a fourth time, or even more often, until the lime is completely dissolved; then it is enough.

Now take [℞] the **Spirit** [⚹] in which the **Gold** [☉] of God, and not of man <note>A common alchemical distinction between "vulgar" gold (common currency) and "philosophical" or "divine" gold.</note>, is dissolved. Put it into a urinal <note>A tall, pear-shaped glass vessel used for digestion and distillation.</note>, place a cap <note>original: "Helm" (alembic head)</note> upon it, and let it pass over gently with a very mild **fire** <term>Fire: Symbolized by △ (Ignis).</term> until the liquid remains. Then you will find at the bottom of the glass the salt of the body; keep this diligently. 

When all this is done, you have rectified your earth well. You should soak <note>original: "imbibiren"</note> the same with the **water** <term>Water: Symbolized by ▽ (Aqua).</term> of its birth in equal parts <note>original Latin: "Ana"</note>. Continue this soaking until your medicine flows upon a glowing silver plate like wax without any smoke. Then you have a Tincture <note>A potent alchemical substance capable of transformation.</note> which truly and justly enters, penetrates, mixes, and coagulates, remaining eternally stable. One part of such a substance transforms for the first time 100 parts of any metal into good **Gold** [☉] or **Silver** <term>Silver: Symbolized by ☽ (Luna).</term> according to the preparation of the work.

# MICHAEL SENDIVOGIUS
## Twelve Treatises
### on the
# Philosopher’s Stone.
## The First Treatise.
### Concerning Nature: what she is, and what kind of people those ought to be who wish to investigate her.

<margin>See the *Turba Philosophorum*, Part 1, page 522. <note>original: "vide Turbam"; the *Turba* is one of the oldest and most influential Latin alchemical texts, presented as an assembly of ancient philosophers.</note></margin>

Many wise and learned people, many hundreds of years ago—indeed, even before the Great Flood, as Hermes <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary Hellenistic figure regarded as the father of alchemy and hermetic philosophy.</note> testifies—have written much concerning the preparation of the <term>Philosopher’s Stone</term> <note>A legendary alchemical substance capable of turning base metals into gold and serving as an elixir of life.</note>, and have left behind so many writings for us that, if Nature did not perform such things every day (which are surely to be believed), almost no one would believe any longer that a Nature even exists. This is because, in ancient times, there were not so many people who invented new things. Indeed, our ancestors, those dear ancients, considered nothing other than Nature and what is possible for Nature; and although they remained upon the simple and humble path and course of Nature, yet

...strives with all its power, and rejoices in reaching its destined end—no different from an ant in its old age, for whom Nature forms wings as it nears its end. In the same way, our minds and senses have climbed so high, especially in the Philosophical Art <note>the art of alchemy</note> or the preparation of the Stone, that we have now almost reached the highest peak. For the Alchemical Art <note>original: "Chymistische Kunst"</note> has invented such subtle things that one could hardly imagine anything higher; and there is such a difference between this modern art and the ancient philosophers, just as there is between a watchmaker and a common blacksmith. For although they both work with iron, neither understands the work of the other, even though each is a master in his own craft. If the father of all philosophers, Hermes <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary foundational figure of alchemy</note>, and the ingenious Geber <note>Jabir ibn Hayyan, an 8th-century polymath and influential alchemist</note>, along with the profound Raymond Lully <note>original: "Raymund Lullio"; a 13th-century philosopher and major figure in alchemical literature</note> were to rise again today, they would not be regarded as philosophers, but rather as mere students by the modern chemists. For they would know nothing of so much distillation, circulation, calcination <term>the process of heating a substance to high temperatures to drive off volatile substances or cause oxidation</term>, and the countless other operations of the artists which people have devised and found in books nowadays. Only one thing is lacking to us, which we ought to know: what they were capable of and what they actually made—namely, the Philosopher's Stone, or the natural Tincture. While we are now seeking after this, we invent other things; and it would be no wonder if the propagation of mankind were not so common...

But so that I may return to my purpose, I have promised that in this first treatise I would explain what Nature is, so that a vain delusion does not lead us away from the simple, true path.

Therefore, Nature is uniquely true, simple <note>original: "schlecht"; in Early Modern German, this meant "plain" or "straightforward" rather than "bad"</note>, and perfect in her essence, whom God created before all time and within whom He has enclosed a spirit. But one should know that the boundary and goal of Nature is God, just as He is also the beginning of Nature; since no thing ends anywhere else than in that wherein it begins. I have stated that there is one single Nature through which God makes all things—not that God could not work anything without her (for He made Nature and is all-powerful)—but it pleased Him to do so, and He made it thus: All things come from this same single Nature, and there is nothing in the whole world outside of this Nature. For although monstrosities <note>original: "Mißgeburten"; refers to biological anomalies or "errors" in the natural process</note> sometimes come forth, this is not the fault of Nature, but rather the fault of either the artist <note>the alchemist or practitioner</note> or the location. This Nature is divided into four places <note>referring to the four classical elements: Earth, Water, Air, and Fire</note> in which she works all that which is seen, as well as that which is in the darkness; since things are much more in the darkness than they should truly appear. She changes herself into the male and the female: and is compared to Mercury <term>Mercury (the element or the deity) symbolizes the volatile, transformative principle in alchemy that mediates between extremes</term>, because she [works] herself at different...

For our part, she is useful in this regard for nothing other than that we know her place and location, which are most fitting and convenient for her—that is, that we know how to unite one thing with another thing according to Nature. This ensures that no human is united with wood, nor a bull or other cattle with a metal, but that each should labor and work within its own kind; then Nature will also do her part. Nature, as mentioned above, has no other place or dwelling than in the will of **GOD**. In the womb, nothing of the seed remains [idle]; rather, after the womb has taken its proper portion, it casts out the rest. It happens in the same way in the *center* of the earth: the magnetic power of a location draws a thing to itself to give birth to its own [specific substance], while the rest is cast out as stones and other waste. For all things have their origin from these same springs, and nothing in this world is brought forth except from these sources.

There are four elements: two heavy and two light, two dry and two moist—but one very dry and one very moist—of male and female gender, etc. Each of these is by its own nature very inclined to bring forth such things that are like itself within its *Sphere* <note>original: "Sphæra"</note> or circle; and so has the Most High ordained it. These four do not rest, but one always drives the other, and each lets its subtle essence or subtlety go, and they meet in the *Center* <note>original: "Centro"</note>.

How this occurs will be seen more extensively in the conclusion of these twelve short treatises.

# The Third Treatise.
## Concerning the True First Matter of the Metals.

The first matter of the metals is twofold, but one without the other completes no metal. The first and most prominent is the moisture mixed with the warmth of the air; this the Philosophers have called <term>Mercury</term> <note>original: "Mercurium"</note>, which is governed by the rays of the sun and moon in the Philosophical Sea. The other is the dry warmth of the earth, which they have called <term>Sulphur</term> <note>original: "Schwefel"</note>. However, because all true philosophers have hidden this latter one the most, we wish to explain it somewhat more clearly—especially the weight, since without the knowledge of it, everything is ruined. 

From this it also follows that many, using a thing which is good in itself, obtain a deformity <note>literally "misbirth" or "monstrosity"</note>, because some take the whole <term>Body</term> <note>original: "Corpus"</note> for the matter, or seed, or <term>Sperm</term> <note>original: "Spermate"</note>, while others take only a piece, and all of these deviate from the path. 

As an example: if someone wanted to take a man’s foot and a woman’s hand together, and from such a mixture try to bring about a human being, it would be an impossible thing. For in every body there is a <term>Center</term> <note>original: "Centrum"</note> and a place—much like the point of the seed or <term>Sperm</term> <note>original: "Spermatis Puncten"</note>—which always makes up only the 1/2800th part, even if it were only a grain of wheat. But the **First Matter** <note>original: "erste Materi"</note> of metals is a moisture mixed with warm air, and it exists in form and shape like a **fatty water** that clings to every single thing, whether it be pure or impure. However, it is more abundant in one place than in another, which happens because the earth in one location is more open, loose, and **porous** (that is, with more air passages) and has a stronger attractive power than in another. Occasionally, it comes to light on its own, clothed in something, particularly in those places where it has nothing to cling to. It is thus recognized because all things take their origin from three sources and general principles, but in the **Matter of Metals**, it comes from only one, without **Conjunction** <note>original: "Conjunction"; the chemical or alchemical joining of substances</note>, except for its clothing or its "shadow," namely **Sulfur**, etc.

## The Fourth Treatise.
### How metals are generated and begotten in the veins of the earth.

Therefore, it is necessary that the <term>pores</term> <note>original: *Pori*; the microscopic openings in matter through which spiritual essences are thought to pass.</note> of the <term>bodies</term> <note>original: *Corpora*; physical substances or forms.</note> be opened so that the <term>sperm</term> <note>original: *Sperma*; here used to mean the visible physical vehicle or fluid that carries the life-spark.</note> may be released, in whose center and midst the <term>seed</term> <note>original: *Saamen*; the invisible, spiritual essence or "spark" of life.</note> lies, which is the air. When the same enters the appropriate <term>womb</term> <note>original: *Mutter*; literally "mother," but used alchemically to refer to the "matrix" or environment where growth occurs.</note>, it is congealed, and it also congeals whatever pure matter it finds, as well as the impure matter mixed among the pure.

As long as the seed is in the body, the body lives (when it is entirely consumed, the body dies; thus all bodies are also weakened when they have released the seed.) Experience also testifies that people who indulge too much in love <note>A reference to the frequent expenditure of seminal fluid, which alchemists believed depleted the body's "radical moisture" or vital spirit.</note> become duller; just as trees that bear too much fruit soon become barren. 

Thus, as has been frequently reported, the seed is an invisible thing, but the sperm is visible; it is almost a living soul, and it is found in no dead or deceased things. One obtains it in two ways: gently and also by force. But because we are here dealing only with its power, I say that nothing is born without seed: through the power of the seed [comes]...

# The Eleventh Treatise.

Now, if you wish to set your mind toward creating a thing (first consider the things already created), if you cannot understand those things that lie before your eyes, much less will you understand what you wish to create and make; for you should know that you can create nothing, as that belongs to **GOD** alone. Meanwhile, it happens that not only the air but also the water slips out, just as can be seen when black clouds are violently hurled into the air. Of this, I have a well-known example for you: let water boil in a pot; with a small fire, you will see a small vapor and wind, but with a stronger fire, a thicker and coarser vapor.

One might say, however: if this were so, it would happen continuously, yet often no wind is noticed at all. ## The Twelfth Treatise.
### Of the Stone and its Virtue.

Hitherto, enough has been treated concerning the production of natural things, of the elements, of the first and second matter <term>Materia; the primary substance or "prime matter" from which the universe was created</term>, of bodies and seeds, and their use and virtue. I have also described the way to make the Philosophical Stone <term>Lapis Philosophorum; the legendary substance capable of transmuting base metals into gold and acting as a universal medicine</term>. Concerning its virtue, however, I will now reveal as much as nature has granted me and experience has disclosed. But in order that I may grasp the entire content of these twelve treatises summarily and in few words, so that the God-fearing reader may perceive my meaning and understanding, the matter is thus constituted.

If anyone should wish to doubt the certainty of this art, let him read the many books of the ancient philosophers grounded in reason and experience, who, as trustworthy men, are not to be mistrusted in their art. Whoever does not believe them is not to be disputed with, as one who contradicts the first principles <term>Principia; the foundational, self-evident truths of a science or philosophy</term>; for the deaf <note>original: "Tauben"; Sendivogius is playing on the biblical metaphor of those who have ears but do not hear.</note>

# Chemical Writings

[Ammo]niac, or <term>philosophical Mercury <note>original: "Mercurii philosophici"; the "living" spirit of metals that alchemists sought to extract, which they believed was the true key to transmutation, distinct from common quicksilver.</note></term> from our **Pontic water**, and the use of the same, has not been so openly revealed; and God alone shall reveal it, he who knows the hearts and minds of men. It is, as mentioned above, necessary to have only one vessel from beginning to end, or at most two; likewise, a **constant fire** is needed in both works, regarding which those who err may read the tenth and eleventh treatises. If you work in the <term>third matter <note>original: "dritten Materi"; a common error in alchemy where practitioners tried to make the Philosopher's Stone from biological substances (like hair or blood) or common minerals rather than the "metallic seed."</note></term>, however, you have failed. Those who deal with such things work outside of this our unique salt, which is **Mercury**, in herbs, animals, stones, and minerals; they work outside of the <term>Sun and Moon <note>original: "Sole und Luna"; alchemical code for gold and silver, the "parents" of the Stone.</note></term>, which are covered with the <term>Circle of Saturn <note>original: "Kreyse Saturni"; Saturn represents lead or the state of "blackness" (nigredo). This suggests that the gold and silver are hidden within a base, leaden, or "corrupted" exterior that must be purified.</note></term>. Whoever desires to reach the longed-for end must know the **transformation of the elements**, making what is light heavy, and making the **spirit not a spirit**; then he will work in no external thing. The fire is the **regiment** <note>original: "Regiment"; the governing rule or management of the heat levels required to guide the chemical reaction through its various stages.</note>; whatever happens there happens through fire, as has been sufficiently said before, and is now said again in place of the conclusion. Fare well, most favorable reader, and enjoy this my work, witnessed through experience, for a long time to the glory of God and the welfare of your soul.

# A Brief Preface / concerning the Dialogue.

Who exactly the writer of this little book may be is unnecessary to know. But as to why he wrote this, hear the reason. It is also of no necessity that you know who I am. Yet know for a certainty, in the highest truth, that the author of this little book knows how to make the **Philosophers' Stone** <note>The legendary "Philosophers' Stone" was the ultimate goal of alchemy, believed to be a substance capable of turning base metals into gold and granting long life.</note>, has made and prepared it, and still has and possesses it. ### Dialogue and Conversation between Nature, Mercury, and an Alchemist.

Once upon a time, the alchemists gathered together and held a general council to discuss how the <term>Philosopher’s Stone</term> <note>The legendary goal of alchemy: a substance believed to be capable of transmuting base metals into gold and providing an elixir of life.</note> should be prepared; they decided among themselves that each one present should offer his own opinion. This assembly took place under the open, free sky, upon a heath, and moreover on a clear day. Many there agreed unanimously that quicksilver or <term>Mercury</term> <note>In alchemical theory, Mercury represents the fluid, feminine, and metallic principle.</note> was the first matter <note>original: *erste Materie*; the fundamental substance from which all things are made.</note>, but others favored <term>Sulfur</term> <note>Sulfur represents the active, fiery, and masculine principle.</note>, while still others proposed something else entirely. Nevertheless, Mercury or quicksilver was the primary topic of debate, especially based on the writings of the philosophers <note>Referring to the "Hermetic philosophers," the established authorities in alchemical literature.</note>, since they identify it as the true matter, as well as the first matter of the metals. Inasmuch as the philosophers cry out and shout, "Our Mercury, our quicksilver!"—indeed, while they were contending with one another in this manner and struggling with particular labor (as each one eagerly awaited the conclusion of this question), a heavy storm occurred in the meantime, with thunder, lightning, and hail, and an unheard-of wind and downpour. This turbulence scattered the assembly, driving each person individually into foreign lands and provinces, dividing and completely separating them, so that the final...

# Preface
## by the *Author* to the Reader.

Since it does not behoove me, Kind Reader, to describe these matters more clearly than other ancient *Philosophers* <term>Philosophers: In an alchemical context, "Philosophers" refers to the "Philosophers by Fire"—those who studied the secrets of nature and the transformation of matter.</term> have done, you will perhaps not be well satisfied with my writings. This is especially likely because you have so many other *philosophical* books at hand. Believe me, however, that it is not necessary for me to write books, since I seek neither profit nor vain glory from them; for this reason, I also do not desire to make known who I may be. 

What I have already allowed to come to the light of day <note>original: "Tag-Liecht"; an early modern idiom for publishing a work or making it public.</note> for your benefit has seemed to me to be more than enough. I had intended for the remainder to be reserved for the *Harmony* <note>The "Harmony" likely refers to a larger, comprehensive work on the systematic arrangement of natural laws, a common project for thinkers of this era.</note>, where I have discoursed at length on natural things. # On Sulfur /
## The Second Principle of Mineral Things.

Sulfur is not the least among the principles and origins of minerals, since it is a part of metal—indeed, the most noble part of the <term>Philosopher's Stone</term> <note>The legendary "Stein der Weisen," a substance believed to be capable of turning base metals into gold and granting eternal life.</note>, about which many ancient philosophers have left behind beautiful, diverse, and true things in their writings. Even <term>Geber</term> <note>Jabir ibn Hayyan (c. 721–c. 813), a prolific Islamic scholar and alchemist whose Latinized works were foundational to European alchemy.</note> himself says in the 28th chapter of the book *The Summary of Perfection* <note>original: "Summarischen Vollkommenheit," referring to the influential Latin text *Summa Perfectionis Magisterii*.</note>: 

> By the most high **GOD**, He <note>In alchemical prose, this likely refers to the "light" or the sulfurous principle itself as a divine agent within matter.</note> illuminates every body: For it is a light from the light, and a <term>tincture</term> <note>In this context, a substance or "dye" that penetrates and transforms the internal nature of a metal.</note>. 

Before we begin to treat of it, however, it seems advisable to us first to describe the derivation of the principles, especially since <term>sulfur</term> has been held from ancient times to be the foremost principle of things. From whence the principles have their origin, however, has been shown by few until now, and it is very difficult to judge any of the principles—as with any matter—if one does not know its derivation and origin. For what does a blind man know of colors? Therefore, what our ancestors omitted, we have undertaken to explain in this treatise.

Now, there are two origins of things, especially of metals, according to the opinion of the ancient philosophers: sulfur and mercury. According to the younger philosophers <note>This refers to the "Paracelsians" or followers of Paracelsus (1493–1541), who added "Salt" to the traditional Aristotelian and Arabic duo of Sulfur and Mercury to form the <term>Tria Prima</term> (Three Principles).</note>, however, there are three: salt, sulfur, and mercury. These origins, however, spring from the four elements, from whose roots we must specifically begin. Thus, the students of this holy science should note that there are four elements: and that each of these four holds another within its center and midpoint, from which it receives its elemental nature. These are the four pillars of the world, which were separated by Divine Wisdom from the mixed <term>Chaos</term> <note>In alchemy, "Chaos" refers to the "Materia Prima" or the unformed, primal state of matter before it is organized into specific substances.</note> during the creation of the world. These pillars also maintain this structure of the world in balance and proportion through their opposing actions, and through the influence of heavenly powers, they bring forth all things both below and above the earth—of which we shall speak in the proper place. We wish to turn to our subject and treat first of the nearest element: Earth.

### Concerning the Element of Earth.

The Earth is an element very worthy in its constitution and majesty. Within this element, the other three rest, particularly fire. It is the preeminent element for hiding and for revealing what has been entrusted to it: it is dense and porous, heavy due to its compactness, yet light by its very nature;

## Of the Element of Air.

Air is a complete element, most magnificent in its property—externally light and invisible, internally heavy, visible, and fixed. It is warm and moist, tempered by the fire, and much more worthy than earth and water. It is indeed volatile, but it can be <term>fixed</term> <note>original: "figirt" or "fix." In alchemy, making a substance "fixed" means rendering it resistant to heat so that it no longer evaporates or changes state.</note>, and when it is fixed, it makes all bodies penetrable. From its purest substance, the vital spirits of animals were created; the middling part was raised into its own sphere; but the remainder, the coarsest part, remained in the water and is <term>circulated</term> <note>original: "circulirt." A process of repeated evaporation and condensation intended to purify and "spiritualize" a substance.</note> with the water, just as fire is with the earth, for they are good friends. It is most magnificent, as mentioned, and the true place and location of the seed of all things. In it, the seed is <term>imagined</term> <note>original: "imaginirt." In this context, "imagination" refers to a formative or creative power that gives a specific "idea" or shape to the raw matter of the seed.</note>—as in a man—and is afterwards cast into its sowing through a circulated impulse. This element possesses a shape and form of wholeness, to distribute the seed into the <term>wombs</term> <note>original: "Gebärmüter." In alchemical theory, various substances or vessels act as "wombs" where the transformation and "birth" of new materials occur.</note> through the sowing

## Of the Element, Fire.

Fire is the purest of all elements and, above all, the most precious, full of an inherent, oily sharpness <note>The "oily sharpness" (feisten Schärfe) refers to the alchemical concept of "Sulfur," the flammable and active principle in matter.</note> that is penetrating and digestive <term>digerirend</term> <note>In alchemy, "digestion" refers to the process of applying a gentle, constant heat to a substance to mature or refine it, mimicking the heat of a stomach or a nesting bird.</note>, acting as a sticky, strong caustic <term>Etzung</term> <note>original: "Etzung." While this often means "etching" in modern German, here it refers to a corrosive or "eating" power, as fire consumes its fuel.</note>. It is visible on the outside but invisible on the inside; it is very fixed, hot, and dry, and it is tempered by the Earth. Its purest substance and essence was, at the very creation of the world, exalted with the throne of Divine Majesty, when the waters of the heavens were established (of which we have already spoken in the section on the Element of Water). From the other, somewhat coarser substance of fire, the **angels** were created. From an even less pure fire, combined with the purest air, the **heavenly lights** and **stars** were made. That which was less pure still was placed in its own sphere to enclose the heavens. However, the impure and oily matter was placed and shut away in the center of the earth by the **Highest Master Craftsman** <note>original: "Werckmeister," a common term for God as the Great Architect or Demiurge of the universe.</note> to drive constant motion; this is what we call the **hellish fire**. 

All these fires are indeed divided, yet they possess a natural union and kinship. This element is the most restful of all, like a **wagon** which rolls forward when it is pulled, but stands still when it is not pulled. It exists imperceptibly in all things. Within it are the lively senses and the understanding, which, at the first infusion of human life, were [divided]—

# MICHAEL SENDIVOGIUS #

[in] Paradise, man was immortal: as all the scribes <note>original: "Schrifftgelehrte"; this refers to biblical scholars or theologians of the time.</note> and the Bible itself testify; nevertheless, no philosopher has brought forth sufficient proof of immortality up to this day, which a seeker of this holy science <note>Refers to Alchemy or "Hermetic Philosophy," often called the Holy Science by practitioners.</note> should know, so that he may see how all things happen naturally and can be understood so easily. This is once and for all true, and the highest truth: that every composite thing in this world is subject to destruction and separation, which separation is called death in the **animal kingdom** <term>animal kingdom: In early modern science, this encompasses all sentient, breathing life, including humans, categorized by the "animal soul" which provides movement and sensation.</term>; yet, since man is also made and created from four elements, how then could he be immortal? That it could happen in a natural way is hard to believe, indeed, it seems entirely supernatural. Up to this point, this has been the subject of debate. But **GOD** inspired <note>original: "eingegeben"; literally "given into" or revealed to the mind.</note> the pious philosophers many hundreds of years ago that this is natural, which you shall understand from us in this way: Paradise was, and is, such a place created by the Almighty Creator of all things from the true, individual elements—yet the purest, most tempered <term>tempered: A state of perfect balance where the four qualities (hot, cold, moist, dry) are so well-proportioned that they do not conflict or cause decay.</term>, and manifested in the highest perfection—so that everything that was in Paradise and created from those same elements is indestructible. There, man was also created from those same indestructible elements, balanced in right proportion, so that he could in no way be destroyed; therefore, he became a partaker of immortality,

### CHEMICAL WRITINGS ###

Since **GOD** undoubtedly created this Paradise for man alone (concerning which we speak more extensively in its proper place in our *Harmony* <note>original: "Harmonie"; likely a reference to a specific treatise or section within the author's collected works, possibly regarding the "Harmonia" of the world or the elements.</note>). However, after man transgressed the commandment of the Most High through the sin of disobedience, he was cast out into this corruptible elemental world <term>elemental world: The world beneath the moon composed of the four changing elements (Earth, Water, Air, Fire), which are subject to decay and strife, unlike the eternal and balanced realm of Paradise.</term>, which **GOD** had created for the wild animals alone. Because man could not live without nourishment, it became necessary for him to seek his sustenance from these corruptible elements. Through this, the pure element of his creation <note>The author suggests that man was originally composed of a "pure" or "fifth" element (Quintessence) that became tainted by consuming earthly food.</note> was infected and gradually brought to ruin and destruction, until one quality overcame the other, and the [resulting] weakness of the entire structure and, ultimately, separation and death followed.

Subsequently, those who were born outside of Paradise from corrupted seed <note>original: "zerstöhrten Saamen"; refers to the inherited mortality and physical degradation passed down through generations following the Fall.</note> within these perishable elements have come much closer to this corruption and death. Since sustenance grown from perishable food cannot be long-lasting, the further mankind is removed from the expulsion from Paradise, the closer they come to destructibility; hence the shortening of human life. It will eventually reach a point where even upbringing <note>original: "Erziehung"; here referring to the process of physical growth to maturity or the time needed to raise a child, which the author fears will be cut short by premature death.</note> will cease because of the brevity of life. 

To be sure, places are found where, due to healthier air and the influence of the stars <note>original: "Gestirn"; early modern science held that the positioning of the planets and stars directly affected the health, temperament, and longevity of people in specific geographic regions.</note>, nature is not so quickly destroyed and people live more naturally. # Of the Three Principles
### of all things.

After the description of the four elements, we proceed to the three principles of all things, which arise from the elements in the following manner.

After Nature received the **fiefdom** <note>original: *Lehen-Recht*, referring to a legal right or feudal grant of territory</note> over this **world-monarchy** from **GOD**, the **Almighty Creator** of all things, she began to distribute the places and lands to each according to their **dignity** and **worth**, and above all things she set the four elements as **Princes** of this world. ...openly kept secret, who would blame them for that, because they addressed their writings only to their **children** <note>original: *Kindern*; this refers to the "Children of the Art," a traditional term for initiated alchemists</note>, and named <term>Sulfur</term> <note>The active, fiery principle of alchemy</note> and <term>Mercury</term> <note>The fluid, passive principle of alchemy; here "Quecksilber"</note> (which is also sufficient for us) as the matter of metals, and indeed even of their Stone. ## On Sulfur.

Among the three principles <term>Principles: Also known as the *Tria Prima* (Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury), these were believed by alchemists to be the fundamental components of all matter</term>, the philosophers have rightly placed sulfur at the forefront as the most precious principle, for within its preparation lies the entire Art. For there are three kinds of sulfur, and one must choose primarily: a tinging <note>Staining or dyeing, referring to the power to change the color of a metal</note> and coloring sulfur; a sulfur that congeals <term>Congeals: to solidify or thicken a liquid, specifically the "fixing" of liquid mercury into a solid state</term> mercury; and the third, which reveals the essence.

Though we should have treated and dealt with this third one first, since we have already released one principle in the form of a dialogue, we are compelled to carry out the others in the same manner, so that we may do justice to each. Sulfur is more mature than the other principles, and mercury is not made hard except through sulfur. Thus, the entire operation in this Art is nothing other than being able to extract a sulfur from metals, with which our mercury in the veins of the earth is hardened into gold and silver. In our work, this sulfur takes the place of the man and is for that reason more highly esteemed, while Mercury <note>original: "Mercurius"</note> takes the place of the woman. From the union and interaction of these two arise the Philosophical Mercuries. In the "Dialogue of Mercury with the Alchemists," we described a general assembly of alchemists where they deliberated,

[Ari]stotle [and his followers] have fallen into bad company: he <note>Referring to the "boy" or Philosophical Sulfur, the active principle of nature</note> has a sister whom he loves very much, and he is also loved by her, for she is to him like his mother. <note>In alchemical allegory, the "sister" or "mother" often represents Mercury, the passive, nourishing matrix that carries the "seed" of Sulfur.</note> **Alchemist:** Lord, is he the same everywhere? **The Voice:** As far as his nature is concerned, he is one and the same, but in prison he is altered; yet his heart is always pure, though his clothes are very stained. <note>An allegory for how the pure essence of a substance is often hidden beneath external impurities or "crusts" of common matter.</note> **Alchemist:** Lord, has he ever been free? **The Voice:** Yes, certainly, especially in those times when the wise men lived, who held great friendship with his mother. **Alchemist:** Who then were they? **The Voice:** Innumerable many; it was **Hermes**, who was entirely at one with his mother; after him many kings and princes, and no less many other wise men, such as in our times **Aristotle**, **Avicenna**, **Paracelsus**, etc., who liberated him. For these were able to loosen his bonds. **Alchemist:** Lord, what did he then give them for his liberation? **The Voice:** Three kingdoms; for when someone releases him and makes him free, he overcomes his guardians (who now rule in his kingdom), binds them, and gives them into the hand of him who liberated him, to be his subjects and to possess their realms also. And what is even more, there is a **Mirror** <note>original: "Spiegel" — the *Speculum Naturae* or Mirror of Nature was a common metaphor for the total, clear understanding of natural laws and the divine plan.</note> in his kingdom, in which one can behold the entire world; whoever looks into this mirror can find and learn therein the three parts of the wisdom of the whole world, <note>This refers to the *Emerald Tablet* of Hermes Trismegistus, which claims that the master of the work possesses the "three parts of the philosophy of the whole world."</note> and will become as wise in these three kingdoms as **Ari-** <note>The text cuts off here, continuing on the next page as "Aristotle."</note>

<summary>The Voice describes the "Sulfur" (the brother) as a pure essence currently imprisoned by impurities, noting that ancient masters like Hermes and Paracelsus once freed him. In exchange for liberation, the Alchemist is promised dominion over the three kingdoms of nature and access to a "Mirror" containing all worldly wisdom.</summary>

# THE WRITINGS OF MICHAEL SENDIVOGIUS
<note>Latin: "Michaelis Sendivogii." Sendivogius (1566–1636) was a famous Polish alchemist and philosopher known for his theories on the "food of life" found in the air.</note>

If our writings do not please you, you may read the easier works of other authors <note>original: "Scribenten."</note>, but with this warning: that they should compare everything they read with the possibility of Nature and attempt nothing against Nature. Do not believe it, even if it were written in the books of the Sages, that fire does not burn, for that is against Nature. But when it is written that fire has the power to dry and to warm, that is to be believed, because it happens in a natural way.

For Nature always agrees with right reason; there is nothing difficult in Nature, and all truth is simple. # Concluding Discourse.

Every seeker of this art <note>The "Art" refers to alchemy—the study of transforming matter.</note> should, above all things, examine with mature consideration the creation, operation, and powers of the four elements <note>The four classical elements: Fire, Air, Water, and Earth.</note> within his process. For if he does not know their origin and nature, he will not arrive at a knowledge of the principles <note>original: "Anfäng." In alchemical theory, these are the "Three Principles" (Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury) that make up all physical matter.</note>, nor will he ever recognize the true matter of the Stone <note>The Philosopher’s Stone, the legendary substance capable of turning base metals into gold and granting long life.</note>; much less will he reach a good end, because every end proceeds from its beginning. He who well knows what he begins, also well knows what he will finish. For the origin of the elements is a Chaos <term>Chaos: In alchemy, this refers to the primordial, unformed state of matter from which God created the universe.</term>, from which God the Creator of all things created and separated the elements, which is the work of God alone.

However, from the elements, Nature brings forth the principles of things, and that belongs—according to the will of God—to Nature alone. Subsequently, from these principles, Nature makes minerals, ores, and all things, from which the artist <note>The "Artist" is the term used for the practicing alchemist who imitates natural processes.</note>, by following Nature, is capable of many wonderful things. This is because Nature brings forth the ores, metals, and all manner of things from these principles—which are **Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury** <term>Tria Prima: The "Three Principles" defined by Paracelsus as the components of all solid matter: Sulfur (the soul/flammability), Mercury (the spirit/fluidity), and Salt (the body/solidity).</term>. Nature does not simply make a metal directly out of the elements, but through the principles, which are a middle ground (between the elements and the metals). Therefore, if Nature does not do it,

In the same way, if there were no sulfurous vegetable power in plants, water would not be coagulated, nor would the vegetable mercury be turned into herbs and trees.

The same must be understood regarding the **Mineral Kingdom**. If, then, through this, **God** <note>original: "GOtt."</note> should enlighten someone's mind, he will only then recognize what a descendant owes to his predecessors, because this science is always discovered through such intellects and minds. After providing such a crystal-clear revelation, we lay this work into the lap of the most high Creator and **God the Lord**, faithfully commending myself and the pious readers to His grace, goodness, and unspeakable mercy.

## Mercury.

I am neither an evil nor a good angel, but rather one of the seven spirits of the planets <note>original: "Planeten Geistern." In alchemical cosmology, planets were believed to have governing intelligences or "spirits" that directed their influence on Earth.</note>, who govern the **intermediate nature** <note>original: "Mittel-Natur." This refers to the mediating realm between the purely spiritual/divine and the physical/material world.</note>, and who are commanded to rule the four distinct parts of the world—namely the firmamental, animal, vegetable, and mineral parts. There are seven of us who, through our skill, lead all earthly powers and the **influence** <note>original: "Influentz." Historically, this refers to the "in-flowing" of celestial energy from the stars and planets into physical matter.</note> of the upper sphere into the three lower parts <note>likely referring to the three lower kingdoms of nature: animal, vegetable, and mineral.</note> through the **ascendants** and **descendants** <note>Astrological terms referring to the rising and setting of celestial bodies, used here to describe the cyclic flow of energy.</note>, and work within them; for the planets cannot descend physically. **Note well:** this is the spirit that actually helps bring forth the internally generative creatures from the creation of the four elements, and whoever understands this will prepare himself for the **Work** <term>The Work (Magnum Opus): the alchemical process of purifying matter to create the Philosopher's Stone.</term>.

## Albert.

I am quite joyful at your high spiritual report; I confess with all my heart the pure truth, that I perceive more foundation in your very clear report than I have found thus far in all the **philosophers** <note>original: "Philosophis" (Latin plural). In this context, it refers to the "Natural Philosophers" or previous alchemical authors.</note>. But I beg you, allow me one more question, and then I will tell you the reason why I have summoned you and declare it properly; I pray you, tell me your name.

## Mercury.

I am called and am the Spirit of the planet, and not of the God, Mercury <note>original: "Mercurii." Mercury refers both to the Roman deity and the planet or its corresponding alchemical metal.</note>. You did not bring me to you through your banishings and conjurations; rather, I have come to you quite voluntarily by God’s permission. Therefore, your circles, candlesticks, and sword, and your other fantasies, concern me less than nothing—since, in any case, a serving spirit is granted by God to every pious person, yet one finds few who make themselves worthy of such a gift. 

Therefore, be no longer terrified by my blackness, for it shall be the beginning of your wealth <note>In alchemy, the "blackness" (nigredo) is the first stage of the transformation of matter, representing the "death" or decomposition of the substance before it can be purified and reborn.</note>. Was it not also completely dark and gloomy at the beginning of Creation? But through the wisdom of the Creator, the light was separated from the darkness. For after the lovely dawn <note>original: "Morgenröth" (Aurora). A significant stage in alchemical transformation symbolizing the transition from darkness to light and the approach of the final goal.</note>, the sun rises beautifully—high, **sanguine** <term>Sanguine: historically meaning blood-red; in alchemy, it refers to the final red stage (rubedo) of the Great Work, signifying perfection.</term>, and fiery red. 

If you now believe my words—even if they are not human, but rather a resonating echo in accordance with my nature—I will kindly listen to you again and instruct you. Now, step out of your circle and let me enter it; sit yourself at the table and write with diligence whatever I shall tell you. You must begin with the reasons why you have thus summoned and desired me; and do not be meddlesome, but plain and brief in your questions.

Chemical Writings.

## Albertus.

In the name of GOD the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, Amen. Since the Most Holy One exists in an inseparable Trinity, and in inseparable Divine Unity, I ask you, Spirit of Mercury <note>original: "Spiritum Mercurii"</note>, that you should tell me the truth. My question is: whether that which the ancient philosophers have written concerning their Stone of the Philosophers, or Tincture, is a physical reality <note>original: "in rerum natura," a Latin phrase meaning "in the nature of things."</note>, or merely a subtle speculation?

## Mercury.

Know that the philosophers have written various things about this one single thing with a careful foresight, so that fools—who only ask and strive for money—and unfaithful, haughty men might be led astray. By this means, the high secrets of nature (the natural forces that accomplish all things), for which many people of both high and low status strive, may remain all the more hidden. But they have not told the truth, nor can they, in any other thing except in one single thing (for all is in all); anything else serves only to mislead the unworthy. Therefore, I tell you the plain truth in brief words: that when they have written in agreement <note>original: "Concordanz." In alchemy, "concordance" refers to the points where different authors agree, which is where the truth is believed to be hidden.</note> concerning their Stone or Tincture, it is a physical reality <note>original: "rerum natura"</note> and certain.

# MICHAEL SENDIVOGIUS,
### Or J. J. D. J., <note>These initials are often associated with Sendivogius’s titles or his pseudonym "Iure Iuratus," though his most famous moniker follows.</note> commonly called the Cosmopolite.
# FIFTY-FIVE LETTERS.

->To the most illustrious and most worthy<-
->new Fellow of the Cabala of<-
->Unknown Philosophers<- <note>The "Unknown Philosophers" (*Philosophes Inconnus*) refers to a tradition of secret alchemical or Rosicrucian societies that claimed to possess hidden wisdom.</note>
->T. S. P. M. S.<-

->*Letter I.*<-

Your letters, and those of your Patron and our Fellow Briquius, <note>Possibly a Latinized form of a French name like "de Brie."</note> were most welcome to me; nor can I express with what great joy they filled me, as they confirmed your enrollment in our Fellowship <note>original: "Sodalitati"</note> and the plan for establishing and expanding it in France. <note>original: "Galliis," literally "the Gauls."</note> Indeed, a vehement desire for this matter has long burned within me, and the outcome cannot be anything but favorable, since you are endowed with such great gifts of mind and good character, as the aforementioned Briquius testifies to me and as I see for myself in your most elegant writings. To this end, therefore, I send to you with a cheerful heart what you requested of me: the statutes of our said Society, expressed in the Latin tongue. I ask that you maintain a scrupulous <note>original: "religiosam," implying a devoted or sacred adherence to the rules.</note> observation of them and make them most highly recommended to future Fellows. Furthermore—

<meta>catchword: opta- (desire/hope)</meta>

<header>MICHAEL SENDIVOGIUS.</header>

I gladly grant and promise you the desired further insights beyond those revealed to you by your Patron regarding the <term>alchemical matter</term> <note>original: "re Alchymica," referring to the substance or "First Matter" used to begin the work</note>, or the theory and practice of the **Philosopher's Stone**. But it is necessary that you yourself, by your own effort <note>original: "proprio Marte," literally "by your own Mars," a Latin idiom meaning by one's own strength or initiative</note>, labor by incessantly reading, speculating, and operating, so that you may, if possible, add what remains to be known to that which has already been revealed. This task will not be difficult for you; for it is easy to open the doors for one who has the key in his hands. However, so that you may achieve this more quickly, I will not delay in explaining the obstacles encountered and directing stray concepts, if you wish to have counsel on whatever occasions arise during your reading. I profess that no secret will be concealed, except those which only visual observation or manual practice can teach. For there are methods and modes in all arts, but especially in ours, which cannot be so precisely described in words that they do not require practical demonstration or experimental inquiry—which, for the most part, fulfills the wishes of those studying philosophy more or less slowly. Your M. S., most ready for all things, asks and beseeches that you hold these warnings most welcome. *Brussels, 9 February 1646.*

### Letter II.

It is not without great reason, Master S., that you seek a selection in such an immense forest of books, both ancient and recent. For few are faithful; or if there are any, they seem either obscure or clashing with one another, for the most part appearing to contradict themselves, although truly...

<header>LETTERS</header>
<sig>Q 3</sig>

...true things <note>This completes the word "vera" from the previous page</note> they perceive and teach, but in a hieroglyphic style according to the custom of the **Cabala** <note>A Jewish mystical tradition that alchemists adapted to encode their secrets in symbols and metaphors</note>. Indeed, our art is purely cabalistic, and it is a sin to rashly entrust it to the wickedness of the Sophists or the carelessness of the imprudent. You may, therefore, with me as your guide, take up the following works from among such a great multitude of books, and set aside all others as useless to you. Since you already possess the little fish ***Echeneis*** <note>original: "Echeneim," the Remora or "sucker-fish." In alchemy, this fish is a symbol for the "Secret Salt" or agent that stops the "volatile" spirit from evaporating, just as the remora was said to stop ships in their tracks</note>, which wanders in such a vast sea—rare, not to say unique—you have no further need to go fishing, but must instead attend to the preparation, seasoning, and cooking of the little fish itself.

### THE PRINCIPAL AUTHORS ARE,

*First*, HERMES <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary founder of alchemy</note>, whose works are of great, indeed of the greatest importance for understanding our matter: but two of his small books—one titled by his later commentators with the posthumous name ***The Crossing of the Red Sea*** <note>original: "Transitus maris rubri"</note>, and the other ***The Arrival at the Promised Land*** <note>original: "Appulsus terræ promissæ"</note>—are to be cherished above the rest. They are very rare and perhaps cannot be obtained anywhere in EUROPE, except in Constantinople among certain **Marranos** <note>Sephardic Jews who were forced to convert to Christianity; here they are identified as keepers of rare esoteric manuscripts</note>, where I turned their pages and copied them out in full to assist my memory.

*Second*, PARACELSUS, whose writings are divine Lights; but if you can find a certain small volume of his called the ***Chemical Psalter, or the Manual of Paracelsus*** <note>original: "Psalterium Chimicum seu Manuale Paracelsi"</note>, you will see all the secrets of the most hidden cabala and demonstrative physics, and the entire doctrine of the alchemical science, with the veil pulled back. This work is not as rare as the preceding ones. For it is found in the ***Vatican Library in Rome*** and in many other places among the students of the Cabala and...

# MICHAEL SENDIVOGIUS

...among the students of true Alchemy among our countrymen, it fell into my hands: it is not, however, a common work, for which reason I have labored over a copy <note>original: "Apographum," a manuscript copy</note> for my own use, as I did with the previous ones. I would gladly share it with you, except that the doctrine we shall hereafter introduce is the same as that which is handed down in these works; indeed, it will be elucidated with a clearer method and in a briefer style in our own Letters. Furthermore, the *Treatise on Tinctures* <note>original: "Tractatus de Tincturis," a work focused on the "Tincture" or the transformative agent of the Philosopher's Stone</note> by the same **Paracelsus** <note>The famous Swiss-German physician and alchemist (1493–1541) who pioneered the use of minerals in medicine</note> is not to be neglected.

*Third*, **LULL** <note>Ramon Llull (c. 1232–1316), a Catalan polymath; many alchemical works were attributed to him after his death</note>: But among all his books, I recommend to you the *Vade mecum* <note>Latin for "Go with me," a handbook</note> and the *Dialogue*, titled *The Tree of Life* <note>original: "Lignum vitæ"</note>, and at the same time his *Testament* and *Codicil*. Nevertheless, these last books—namely the *Testament* and *Codicil*—and the infinite volumes by the same Author, no differently than those of **GEBER** <note>The Latinized name of Jabir ibn Hayyan, the father of Islamic alchemy</note> and **ARNALDUS DE VILLANOVA** <note>A 13th-century Catalan physician and alchemist</note>, create an inexplicable labyrinth of fictions and useless recipes, from which I myself could scarcely extract and vindicate the truth.

There are also, finally, other collected writings of the ancient Philosophers brought together; these are not unlearned indeed, but they are mixed with sophistries <note>Deceptive or false arguments intended to mislead the unworthy</note>, such that they cannot easily be distinguished from authors of proven reliability.

Among the writers of the middle age, **Bonus** <note>Petrus Bonus, author of the "Precious Pearl"</note>, **ZACHER** <note>Nicholas Flamel's contemporary or a reference to the author of the "Opusculum Chemicum"</note>, **BERNARD, COUNT OF TREVISO**, **ROGER BACON**, and the **ANONYMOUS** *Collector of Sentences* or ***The Rosary of the Philosophers*** <note>original: "Rosarium Philosophorum," one of the most famous illustrated alchemical texts</note>, seem to me to be of a proven spirit and successful doctrine.

### LETTERS.

<margin>Q 4</margin>

Among the most recent authors, I judge none worthy of mention except the Frenchman **FABRE** <note>Pierre-Jean Fabre (1588–1658), a French physician and alchemist who attempted to reconcile chemical medicine with traditional philosophy</note> in his most recently published books; for his earlier works are erroneous and full of falsehoods, though he does include some orthodox <note>meaning "correct" or "standard" in a chemical sense</note> views.

I also include the Author of *Nature Restored* <note>original: *Physica restituta*; this refers to Jean d'Espagnet (1564–1637), a French jurist and alchemist</note>, whose work is interwoven with many deceptive sentences. But if you wish to grasp at the very entrance a full knowledge of true, not counterfeit, science, let our own *New Chemical Light* <note>original: *Novum Lumen Chymicum*, the most famous work attributed to Michael Sendivogius</note> suffice for you, along with the *Treatise on Sulfur* <note>original: *Tractatus de Sulphure*</note> and the *Dialogue of Mercury* <note>original: *Dialogismus Mercurii*</note>. For nothing is missing from these, and they must be turned over in the mind with great attention not once, but a hundred times, because—in the manner of the ancient Philosophers—many things there are written out of order, and several contradictions are even intentionally introduced in various places. Some of these locations provide their own solution and reconciliation in express words, but only in scattered sentences. 

Use these. FAREWELL. *Brussels, February 25, 1646.*

For although that booklet is erroneous in its more important precepts, it nevertheless demonstrates to me the great genius of the author. Your doubts and questions, however, demonstrate the sharpness of your own intellect and

### *Letter IV.*

The last [letter] of Your Lordship promised a judgment concerning the **PAGELIAN** discipline <note>referring to the teachings of an alchemist named Pagelius, possibly a contemporary or an alias used in this correspondence</note>; therefore, in the present letter and those following, we will touch upon it as much as we are able. We will promptly explain what in this is true and, conversely, what is false and erroneous, what must be added more explicitly to its true doctrine, and what must be substituted for its false canons <note>technical rules or standards</note>.

Your Pagelius, then, rightly divides the entire treatment he undertakes into two chapters, according to the rite and method of the Philosophers.

**FIRST**: *Concerning the natural production of all things, but especially of minerals.*

**SECOND**: *Concerning the Art and the preparation of the Philosopher’s Stone, by whose aid and benefit gold and silver are produced.*

*What he teaches in the first chapter does not depart far from the truth, but it is compressed in too narrow a style for it to be able to instill a sufficient knowledge of natural principles and a firm <note>original: "non ancipitem," meaning unwavering or certain</note> faith in its readers.*

<summary>This page concludes a letter with a promise to defend the author's chemical propositions and begins Letter IV, which critiques the alchemical theories of Pagelius. The author acknowledges Pagelius's correct structural approach to natural mineral production and the Philosopher's Stone but finds his writing style too brief to be truly instructive.</summary>

<header>LETTERS.</header>

The second chapter, however, contains one thing consistent with the best discipline—namely, a judgment concerning the general principles of the Stone <note>original: "Lapidis," referring to the Philosopher's Stone</note>. In this, he establishes a certain Mercury different from common mercury <note>original: "Mercurio vulgi," the liquid metal found in nature</note> or mineral activity, as long as it is not yet specified or determined in any of the families of the "lowest mixtures"—that is, minerals, vegetables, and animals. Conversely, he establishes a certain Sulfur alien to the common combustible and foul kind; instead, it is determined under some specific form within one of the aforementioned classes of mixtures, which it can impress upon and communicate to the said Mercury by way of fermentation. He constitutes this as the matter for the said stone; nearly everything else is false and to be rejected, as we shall see hereafter. FAREWELL. Brussels, March 15, 1646.

---

->Letter V<-

Order requires, [Dear Sir], that we defer the first article of the second chapter of the Pagelian booklet <note>original: "PAGESIANI libelli," referring to the work of the author being critiqued</note>, which deals with the investigation of the Mercurial source.

It is certain and undisputed among all Philosophers that the true Mercury—the material principle of mineral things and especially of metals—is a proximate <term>humor</term> <note>a fluid or moisture that serves as a fundamental building block in alchemical theory</note> or a hot, moist vapor, as we shall teach after our examination of the Pagelian work. Therefore, that Mercury is no longer to be sought in a cold, moist source of pure elementary water, as Pagelius concludes; rather, it must be sought from a hot, moist body and substance on account of the dominance of "congealed air" <note>original: "aëris congelati," likely referring to a gaseous substance fixed into a solid or liquid state</note>, such as <term>our matter</term> <note>original: "materia nostra," the secret starting material used by alchemists to begin the Great Work</note> is, which you are now not ignorant of. From which [it is] easy

### *Letter VI.*

The second article of the PAGELIAN work attempts to repeat the method of extracting and subsequently preparing Mercury—a method more mysterious than is fitting—drawing from the misunderstood authority of LULLY <note>referring to Ramon Lull, a medieval scholar whose name was frequently attached to alchemical texts</note> and the poorly applied teachings of other Philosophers. He commands that through distillation, the first tenth part of his <term>magnesia</term> <note>a term for the "raw material" of the Great Work, often looking like a dark mineral</note> to rise first should be kept as the only useful and purely mercurial substance, while the nine remaining parts produced by continuing the distillation should be discarded as useless. But this is done so that, as finally stated, the tenth part might be restored to the reserved third of the residue remaining after the distillation is complete (which he foolishly claims to be the Earth, Salt, and Sulfur of Mercury) and united through repeated <term>cohobations</term> <note>the process of redistilling a liquid by pouring it back onto its solid residue to concentrate it</note>, burials <note>original: "inhumationes," a slow heating process where the vessel is buried in a warm medium like horse dung</note>, digestions, and sublimations described by him. However, he is gravely mistaken; for what the Authors teach concerning the tenth part containing the spirit and concerning

...and concerning burials in their own earth, this refers to something other than the extraction and preparation of Mercury, as will be demonstrated elsewhere at some time. No rule should be applied to the said extraction and preparation of Mercury except the simple distillation of <term>Magnesia</term> <note>in alchemy, a "raw material" or base mineral rather than the modern element magnesium</note>, through which the spirit and oil are raised together until the dregs are dry, followed by the separation of the spirit from the oil and the rectification <note>the process of refining a liquid by repeated distillation</note> of that same spirit, repeated many times. But we shall provide these procedures most fully in their proper place within the "Method of Operation." FAREWELL.

### Letter VII.

Next come the third and fourth articles of the Pagelian <note>original: *PAGESIANI*, referring to the author Pagel, whose work is being critiqued</note> writings. One of these assigns the mineral source for the Sulfur needed for the "work of the philosophers" and proves it; indeed, there is no mineral source for that sulfur other than the one he indicates: namely, gold or silver.

The other article describes the extraction of said Sulfur from the "bowels" <note>the inner essence or core</note> of gold and silver. However, he describes this quite poorly because he prescribes a solvent that is foreign <note>original: *heterogeneum*</note> to gold or silver and therefore violent. Specifically, he suggests a certain "oil" made from common Mercury that has been sublimated multiple times, prepared with <term>sal ammoniac</term> <note>ammonium chloride, used in alchemy as a powerful flux or solvent</note> through <term>deliquescence</term> <note>the process of a solid turning into a liquid by absorbing atmospheric moisture</note>. This is contrary to the intention of Nature. Nature intends for gold and silver to be dissolved—to achieve the creation of the <term>Stone</term> <note>The Philosophers' Stone</note>—in a gentle water that is of the same nature as them, possessing a "homogeneity of principle" (as the <term>Cabala</term> <note>referring to a tradition of mystical or hidden knowledge</note> calls it), rather than a "homogeneity of result," as some falsely suggest. These people are no less mistaken than Pagelius himself, that

<meta>This page continues the critique of the "Pagelian" method for extracting sulfur from precious metals, arguing that only a "homogenous" solvent—the philosophers' mercury—can properly dissolve gold and silver without violence.</meta>

<page-num>248</page-num>
<header>MICHAEL SENDIVOGIUS</header>

...is of the same nature as the matter or substance from which gold and silver are directly and immediately made. This matter is considered in a state of lesser composition <note>a simpler, more primal state of matter before it becomes a specific metal</note>, which it possessed before it coalesced into gold or silver. For there are several subordinate degrees of composition for mixtures, as will be seen later, but it is not of the same nature as gold itself, or "archetypal" silver. And yet, no other substance in the nature of things can possess such <term>homogeneity</term> <note>original: *homogeneitatem*; having the same essential nature or origin</note> of principle with gold or silver except our mercury drawn from <term>magnesia</term> <note>in alchemy, a "raw material" or base mineral rather than the modern element magnesium</note>. This, as you know, is only just elicited, because it is a moist, hot vapor not yet "determined" <note>in alchemical theory, a substance is "determined" once it has been fixed into a specific kingdom—animal, vegetable, or mineral—and can no longer become something else</note> into any family of the lower mixtures—that is, the mineral, vegetable, or animal kingdoms. 

Therefore, it is of a simpler degree of composition than gold or silver or any other lower mixture. All other things, and especially the <term>common mercury</term> <note>original: *mercurius vulgi*; everyday quicksilver used by tradesmen, which alchemists considered "dead" or "fixed" compared to their "living" mercury</note> which Pagelius uses, are already determined into the aforementioned families. Because of this, although many substances seem to share "symbolic conditions" <note>superficial similarities or shared qualities</note> with gold and silver, they are nonetheless <term>heterogeneous</term> <note>original: *heterogenea*; of a different or foreign nature</note> to them. This is because they possess a "specific difference" from gold and silver, having a nature that is opposite even under a different species of the same degree of composition; it is in this opposition that heterogeneity consists.

Therefore, our mercury—not the common kind—must be employed as the solvent for gold and silver and as the agent for extracting their sulfur. This is the error of Pagelius. FAREWELL. March 30, 1646.

### *Letter VIII.*

The fifth article of D. S. suggests that the preparation or composition of the <term>philosophical egg</term> <note>original: *ovi philosophici*; a glass vessel shaped like an egg, used to contain the alchemical matter during its transformation</note> be made from about one ounce of the <term>sulfur</term> <note>in alchemy, sulfur represents the "soul" or active principle of a metal</note> of gold or silver and a very small quantity of his own mercury. He intends to drive and force the spirit into the said sulfur through many repeated <term>distillations</term> and <term>cohobations</term> <note>original: *cohobationes*; the process of repeatedly pouring a distilled liquid back onto its solid residue to concentrate its power</note>. He then intends to save all the moisture afterwards. This, however, argues against the very light of nature and creates a monster: he wants the "egg yolk" or the ferment (that is, the sulfur of gold or silver) to many times exceed the "egg white" or the fermentable matter (that is, the mercury). He removes the natural and necessary moisture required for the result of generation, yet he still expects the <term>physical chick</term> <note>original: *pullum physicum*; a metaphor for the Alchemical Stone or "Great Work" emerging from the vessel</note> to come forth from it, or a <term>cobaltic coagulum</term> <note>original: *coagulum cobaliticum*; a solid mass, here used somewhat dismissively to describe a failed or base result</note> to be formed. Just how foolish the imagination of Pagelius <note>original: *PAGESII*; likely a reference to the alchemist Balthasar Pagelius</note> is in this article is not necessary to exaggerate, as even a simpleton could not fail to perceive it. FAREWELL. BRUSSELS, 5 April 1646.

### Letter XII.

First, therefore, <note>D.S. is likely an abbreviation for a formal salutation like *Dilecte Socie* (Dear Associate) or *Domine Spectabilis* (Respected Sir)</note> God created from nothing the **second matter**, which was not entirely without form (as the foolish pseudo-philosophers imagine), but under the form of **primordial water**, or the element and first-principle properly so-called.
