[mer]cury, which are properly parts of a **mixture** <term>mixtum: a chemical compound or any composite physical substance.</term>, as we have suggested elsewhere.

**Accidental parts** <note>original: "Contingentes partes"</note> are those whose separation diminishes the substance of the mixture but does not truly destroy the mixture itself. These are of two kinds: **Homogeneous** and **Heterogeneous**.

**Homogeneous** parts are simply quantitative; they share the same essence as the whole. Their division only reduces the quantity of the substance—as if, for example, several ounces were removed from a pound of **Gold** <note>original: "Solis" (of the Sun)</note> or **Silver** <note>original: "Lunæ" (of the Moon)</note>.

**Heterogeneous** or integral substances are those that have a different nature from one another and from the whole. Their total separation destroys the whole substance, and they can never be recombined. However, the destruction of only some of these parts merely mutilates the substance without destroying it.

All these kinds of parts apply to all mixtures—from the lowest of the **three families** <note>The "three families" or kingdoms: mineral, vegetable, and animal.</note> to the highest and middle **originated principles** <note>original: "principiis principiatis," referring to the primary building blocks of matter that have begun to take on specific qualities.</note> that have not yet been condensed into specific species. *But they do not apply equally; for in some, a greater quantity of **sulfur** exists, which are consequently called "sulfur" by the Philosophers in a broad sense, because the name is taken from the majority part—in the same way that gold is frequently called and signified by the name "sulfur." In others, **mercury** dominates, and those take the name of mercury. In others, **salt** exceeds, and these are called salts. Yet in solid and especially "well-cooked" <note>original: "coctis," referring to the alchemical process of maturation or refinement through heat.</note> bodies, Salt and Sulfur are one and the same, or at least they cling together so closely that they can scarcely be separated.*

It further explains that alchemists name substances based on which of the three principles—Salt, Sulfur, or Mercury—is most dominant.</summary>

...which is why the Ancients rarely or never spoke of **Salt**; but when substances are reduced into **vitriol** <term>vitriol: a sulfate mineral, often used in alchemy to describe a substance's acidic or glassy state.</term>, the power and name of salt fits them best. ### Letter LII.

In the aforementioned definitions, the meaning of the Distinguished Scholar <note>original: "D. S.", likely referring to a specific teacher or the author's own previous doctrine.</note> concerns either the substance of each partial matter—namely, the **vitriol of Gold** <note>original: "vitriolo Solis" (vitriol of the Sun/Gold)</note> and our specified **universal spirit**—or it concerns the **subject** in which both matters exist and from which they are drawn, namely from simple mineral Gold or our **Magnesia** <term>Magnesia: in alchemy, this refers not to the chemical element magnesium, but to the "Mother of Metals" or the primary raw material used to create the Philosopher's Stone.</term>.

If we consider the substance itself, we look either at the **waste parts** <note>original: "partes excrementitias"</note> or the **natural parts**. Regarding the waste parts, none are to be removed, because none exist as waste; this is due to the perfect tempering of the one—namely the vitriol of Gold—and the simplicity of the other—namely our universal spirit.

If, however, we look at the **natural parts**, their separation should not even be attempted. This is because separation is impossible without the destruction of the **mixture** <term>mixtum: a chemical compound or composite substance.</term>. Even if such a separation were possible, it would be useless and superfluous; for as has been stated and proven, it is against nature for them to return to the body together again, whether in quantity or in kind.

But if the meaning concerns the "subject" of both matters and we look at the waste parts, one must indeed be wary of something—namely the **earthiness** <note>original: "terrestreitas"</note> or superfluous earth. This earth is confused with the substance itself during the production of salt, and in the formation of our magnesia, it is mixed with the universal spirit...

Contemplate, therefore, how the text of the said first chapter of Genesis, in its first few lines of introduction, briefly touches upon the general parts of the physical world...

...[the origin] of things, namely heaven and earth, also teaches that the parts or operations of the beginning of the **Mastery** <note>original: "magisterii", referring to the process of creating the Philosopher's Stone</note> consist in this: namely, that from **chaos** <note>original: "chao"; here, the raw, unrefined matter of the alchemical work</note> (not indeed the first primordial chaos, for that pertains to creation and the Creator; but a secondary, material chaos), first our water or our universal spirit—enveloped in the darkness and gloomy confusion of **Magnesia** <term>Magnesia: in alchemical texts, this is not the modern element magnesium, but a name for the "prime matter" or the crude mineral substance containing the "seed" of gold</term>, over which the **Azothian spirit** <term>Azoth: the essential transformative spirit or "universal solvent" sought by alchemists, often identified with the spirit of Mercury</term> (a created and corporeal type and image of the uncreated spirit) broods—so that the heaven and the earth of the **Philosophers** <note>original: "Philosophorum", the traditional title for alchemists</note> may be made at once, coalescing while empty and void like the silt in a spring and the **Salt** in the sea, finally to be made fruitful with seeds by the action of the Azothian spirit, moved artificially by external fire. **First**, let there be light, and let it be divided from the darkness which is upon the face of the **philosophical abyss**, and let day be separated from night, so that they may then succeed one another through all other operations; for in the whole work, light and darkness must necessarily take turns.

**Secondly**, let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters, and let the waters be divided from the waters—namely, those which are under the firmament from those which are above the firmament—that is, the **thick from the subtle**; and let those be gathered into one place, so that the dry land may appear.

This concludes the discussion concerning the matter and the manner of acting; in what follows, we shall hereafter deal with the terms <note>original: "terminis"; here referring to the specific definitions and technical vocabulary of alchemy</note>. Farewell.

### *Letter LIII.*

Those things which pertain to the terms, Dear Friend <note>original: "D. S.," likely an abbreviation for "Dilecte Socie" (Dear Companion) or a specific recipient's title</note>, are reduced to two headings. The first concerns **compound terms**, and the other **simple terms**.

**Compound terms** are descriptions which the Philosophers <note>Alchemists often referred to themselves as "Philosophers" or "Sons of Art"</note> use to indicate the matter and the manner of acting, but especially to demonstrate the matter. These are reduced to two articles, of which the first regards the **primary matter** <term>primary matter: "materia prima"; the original, undifferentiated substance required to begin the alchemical Work</term>, and the other the **secondary matter** <term>secondary matter: "materia secunda"; the substance after it has undergone its first stage of processing or "purification"</term>.

Descriptions which pertain to the primary matter are divided into **univocal** <note>terms that have a single, direct meaning</note> and **analogous**.

**Analogous** descriptions are those by which the **sun** <note>original: "sol"; in alchemy, this refers to gold or the solar, masculine principle of the Work</note>—in the state and condition in which it is submitted by the Philosophers as the primary matter of the **Stone** <note>The Philosopher's Stone</note>—is depicted, but under the names of different headings. These names partly share a similar nature with the sun and partly a different one, just as **living sulfur** <term>living sulfur: "sulphur vivum"; native or "virgin" sulfur, believed to be a fundamental building block of metals</term> is called **vitriol** <term>vitriol: "vitriolum"; while usually referring to sulfate salts, in alchemy it often served as an acronym (V.I.T.R.I.O.L.) or a hidden name for a corrosive solvent</term>, and it is in this sense that the following pronouncement ought to be understood.

Vitriol and our **dissolved gold** <note>original: "solutum aurum nostrum"</note>, or the **solar earth**, is a metallic vitriol that corresponds through a certain analogy and proportion with all vitriols. Descriptions of this kind are innumerable—sometimes through a similarity of causes, sometimes through the identity of certain properties, sometimes through the conformity of effects and actions, and sometimes through the equality of accidents <note>In Aristotelian philosophy, "accidents" are the outward, non-essential characteristics of a thing, like color or smell</note>...

...references occur everywhere throughout the Authors, such as when the **Sun** <note>original: "Sol"; in alchemy, this represents the solar, masculine principle or gold</note> is called a curdling agent, a leaven, the yolk of the philosophical egg, or the male.

Univocal descriptions <note>terms with a single, direct meaning</note> are those which designate the Sun by name through the qualities and attributes most proper to it, precisely explaining its entire essence and that alone. ### *Letter LIV.*

The second article, Dear Friend <note>original: "D. S.," likely abbreviating "Dilecte Socie" (Dear Companion)</note>, comprising descriptions of the **secondary matter** <term>secondary matter: "materia secunda"; the substance after it has undergone its first stage of processing or purification</term>, is subdivided into three parts.

The first concerns the descriptions of the secondary matter itself.

The second considers the descriptions of the **subject** <note>the physical source or host material</note> in which it exists and from which it must be sought.

The third contains descriptions which pertain to both in common: namely, to the substance of the secondary matter itself and its subject.

The first [descriptions] are either **univocal** or **analogous**.

The **analogous** <note>metaphorical or symbolic</note> descriptions are very numerous; they are sufficiently distinguished by themselves by considering whether they describe the nature of our matter more broadly or more narrowly than is fitting for that to which they refer. Such descriptions are handled in the discussion of simple terms, which are omitted here for the sake of brevity.

<note>original: "MICHAELIS SENDIVOGII"; Michael Sendivogius (1566–1636) was a famous Polish alchemist and physician known for his theories on the "food of life" found in the air.</note>

Univocal descriptions <note>terms with a single, direct meaning</note> are also diverse, such as the statement affirming that our matter is found in every place, exists in all corporeal things, and is openly present before the eyes of everyone. Yet, you do not perceive it to be "vile" <note>common or worthless</note>, even though it is found in dungheaps <note>original: "sterquiliniis"; alchemists often claimed their secret was hidden in common waste to emphasize its omnipresence and the "base" nature of the starting material</note>. Nevertheless, it is considered the hidden food of life. How all these things are to be understood, and how they apply only to the universal spirit, has been sufficiently suggested in the preceding Letters.

The descriptions of the second part are likewise either **Analogous** or **univocal**.

The **Analogous** <note>symbolic or metaphorical</note> descriptions are those by which the subject of the secondary matter is called **Talc** <term>Talc: in alchemy, not the modern mineral, but a term for a white, shimmering, or "fixed" substance</term>, **foliated earth** <term>terra foliata: the purified earth or "salt" of the matter after it has been refined into a flaky or leaf-like state</term>, **honey**, **dew**, the **mercury of the Philosophers**, the **mineral**, the **pit**, and many others.

**Univocal** <note>literal</note> descriptions are rare, and among six hundred volumes we have found only three or four. These are indeed so clear and transparent that clearer ones could not be given, though they are not obvious at the very first glance.

The **first** is that which asserts the name of our subject produces the same sound—or one only slightly changed—in all known regions and languages, whether living or obsolete. This is because at least the first syllable everywhere has an equal sound and effect of letters.

The **second** is that which says the name of our subject is completed by **three letters and five characters**. This is because, in the Latin idiom, as well as the Greek and Hebrew, it is written with only three letters of a different kind, and two of the same kind combined with two of the preceding. <note>This is a classic alchemical riddle. Sendivogius is likely referring to "SAL" (Salt), which in various scripts or symbolic permutations (like "SALIA" or "S-A-L") fits his numerical wordplay.</note>

The third [category] is that in which it is said that the aforementioned **subject** <term>subjectum: the physical raw material from which the alchemist begins their work</term> is represented by a single **mystical character** <term>character mysticus: a symbolic sign or sigil used to hide the identity of a substance from the uninitiated</term>. To this character, five letters expressing its name can be related—whether the whole is distributed and divided into parts similar to the said characters, or composed of the five aforementioned similar partial characters. <note>original: "unico charactere mystico figurari"</note>

You will be able to verify the aforementioned descriptions as you please, since the name is known to you. However, you should rather consider the qualities of that subject and the **liquor** <note>the liquid essence or "mercury" extracted from the raw material</note> which is drawn from it, so that you may confirm within yourself the opinion we have passed down to you on this matter and fix it deeply in your mind.

The third part concerns **mixed descriptions** that encompass both the substance of the matter and its subject. You could note many such descriptions similar to those by which the **Philosophers** <term>Philosophers: a standard term for alchemists, who considered their work a form of natural philosophy</term> testify that their "thing" is neither vegetable, nor mineral, nor animal; nor is it drawn or derived from them. <note>original: "nec vegetabilem, nec mineralem; nec animalem esse"</note> But our discourse would exceed the limits of these **Letters**; moreover, it is not our plan or intent here to gather all descriptions of every nature in their proper place, but rather to provide light for distinguishing between them.

Regarding descriptions of the **mode of acting** <note>original: "modi agendi"; the specific laboratory procedures or chemical manipulations</note>, we shall say nothing, even though our classification might require it. Enough and more has been said about these in the final part of the chapter on the mode of acting. **Farewell.**

### *Letter LV.*

Now we must deal with simple terms. Therefore, the entire ambiguity regarding simple terms, or of simple terms themselves, revolves around the "homonymy" <note>words that sound the same but have different meanings</note> of various things and operations. That is, it lies in the different application of the same name to various things, or the "polyonymy" <note>using many names for one thing</note> of the same thing when it is considered or produced in different ways.

According to this homonymy, our **universal spirit**—before it is received into our <term>magnesia</term> <note>In alchemy, "magnesia" refers not to the modern chemical, but to the "raw material" or "mother" substance that contains the metallic seed</note>, which we call its subject—is named the <term>Mercury of the Philosophers</term>. This is not meant in a simple sense, but by way of the proportion and analogy it shares with the <term>Planet Mercury</term>. Just as that planet, when joined with each and every other planet, takes on their qualities and nature, so too does our <term>Mercury</term> act with the "inferior planets"—namely the metals, or the seeds of metals and other mixtures. This is something that the <term>common mercury</term> <note>original: "Mercurius vulgi"; ordinary quicksilver bought from a merchant</note> cannot provide; for although it is joined to the substance of metals through amalgamation, it can never, by any artifice, take on their qualities—at least not in regards to the <term>multiplication of seeds</term> <note>the process of increasing the power and quantity of the alchemical essence</note>.

It is called by the same name while it resides in the aforementioned <term>magnesia</term>, or as soon as it has been drawn out from it, or when, after undergoing "corruption" <note>the stage of breaking down or putrefaction</note> in the <term>philosophical egg</term> <note>the sealed glass vessel used to incubate the alchemical matter</note>, it revives and is intimately blended and identified with <term>gold</term>.

You can judge which thing—and in what state—should be understood when the term occurs here and there, by considering whether you have a part of *Theory* or of *Practice* before your eyes.

He specifically distinguishes "Philosophical Mercury" from "common mercury" by its ability to take on the qualities of other metals.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the discussion by Michael Sendivogius regarding alchemical terminology, specifically focusing on "polyonymy"—the use of many different names for the same substance depending on its current state or the specific operation being performed.</meta>

<page-num>347</page-num>
<header>LETTERS.</header>

---

The same is said of the gold which is called the <term>leaven</term> <note>original: *fermentum*; a substance that, like yeast, triggers a transformation in a larger mass</note> in the <term>Philosophical Egg</term> <note>the sealed glass vessel used in the alchemical process</note>; it is called by this same name when it is in the state of the <term>perfect stone</term> and during the act of <term>projection</term> <note>the final stage where the Stone is cast upon base metals to transform them into gold</note>.

According to the principle of <term>polyonymy</term> <note>the practice of giving many names to one thing</note>, the aforementioned **Mercury** is named according to its various states and operations. At times it is called **antimony**, when, during the aforementioned solution, it purifies the gold and makes it most subtle in the manner of common antimony; yet this substance is far more noble and powerful. At other times it is called **Saturn** <note>the alchemical name for lead</note> while in the Philosophical Egg, according to its degree of metallic form—or rather, because its temperament is shared with the symbol of Saturn. At times it is called **female** while it receives the seed of gold. At other times it is called a **magnet**, because through a certain magnetic virtue it attracts the specific seed of gold. In the same way, it is called **steel** <note>original: *chalybs*</note>, because just as a magnet attracts steel, so does the seed of gold attract the aforementioned Mercury.

Furthermore, it acquires the names of **sulfur**, **salt**, and **leaven**, whether in the preparation of the <term>magistery</term> <note>the completion of the "Great Work" or the Philosopher's Stone</note>, in its multiplication, or at various other times and operations. Specifically, it is called **sulfur** when the <term>central fire</term> <note>the internal heat or vital spark within the matter</note> changes its cold temperament and the heat takes command. It is called **salt**, however, when the dryness of the fire and earth lies in balance with the moisture—one being the master of the other—and the substance reaches such a state of consistency that it can be dissolved equally in fire and water without any loss, yet in clear air and earth, it becomes hard like the sun. Finally, the said Mercury is called **leaven** in that state where it is itself coagulated and solidified so that it may make another like itself, both...

Although the ancient philosophers <note>In this context, "philosophers" refers to early alchemists and natural scientists.</note> wrote about this science in various ways, and hid the true beginnings of the art under almost countless names; they nevertheless did so not without great and weighty consideration, as we intend to explain hereafter. And though they spoke of it in many different ways, they are by no means in conflict or opposed to one another: rather, they all aim for a single goal, and speak of one thing. However, they saw fit above all to name the <term>Proper Agent<note>original Latin: "Proprium Agens"; refers to the primary active force or substance that triggers the alchemical transformation.</note></term>, or the actual working principle, with strange names that were at times entirely contrary to its nature and properties.

# Of Abbot Synesius

Therefore take heed, my son, that the great God created two stones within this *Universe* <note>original: "Universo"</note>, namely a white and a red one, both of which are contained within a single *Subject* <note>In alchemy, the "subject" refers to the base raw material from which the Work begins.</note> and thereafter grow in such abundance that anyone can take as much of them as they themselves desire. And their *Material* <note>original: "Materia"</note> is so constituted that it holds the middle ground between the metals and *Mercury* <note>original: "Mercurio"; refers here to "philosophical mercury" or quicksilver, the fluid principle of matter.</note>, and it is partly <term>fixed<note>A substance is "fixed" if it can withstand fire without evaporating or changing.</note></term> and partly <term>unfixed<note>original: "unfix"; also known as volatile; a substance that evaporates or transforms easily when heated.</note></term>; otherwise, it would not hold the middle between the metals and the Mercury. This *Material* is the instrument or tool that fulfills our desire when we prepare it.

Therefore, all those who work in this art without this *Medium* <note>The "medium" or middle-agent acts as a bridge between the spiritual and physical aspects of the work.</note> or middle-agent lose their labor. If they understood this *Medium*, however, all things would be easy for them and would turn out well.

Know that this *Medium*, because it is of an aerial nature, is found among the heavenly bodies; in it alone are the male and female genders properly to be found, and it possesses a firm, strong, fixed, and permanent virtue <note>In this context, "virtue" refers to an inherent power or medicinal property.</note> within it. ### Chemical Writings

...[from the earthly] filth, which is greed, through which the ignorant have tethered their noses to the earth of this world (which, without this wondrous <term>Fifth Essence<note>original: "Quinta Essentia"; the purest, most concentrated essence of a substance, believed by alchemists to be the life-force of matter.</note></term>, is a house of utter poverty), might be heard as being cleansed. This is done in the confidence that these divine souls, once they have penetrated to the bottom of the <term>Democritean Well<note>A classical metaphor for the "depths of truth." Alchemists used this to describe the deep, hidden secrets of nature that are difficult to access.</note></term>—that is, into the truth of nature—would undoubtedly recognize the great confusion and disruption that would befall all social orders and trades if every person were able to make as much money as they themselves desired.

And for these reasons, they chose to speak through figures, symbols, and parables, so that they might be understood only by those souls who are discerning, holy, and enlightened by wisdom. Nonetheless, in the books they have compiled, they have provided a certain path, road, and rule through which the discerning person may grasp everything they have written in a hidden manner, and finally reach the goal after making several errors—as I, praise God, have done.

### Of Abbot Synesius

...that they have always spoken truthfully, but in a very concealed manner, at times even through fables, which I intend to clearly resolve and reveal to you in this small book in such a way that every person eager for this science will be able to understand that which the <term>philosophers<note>In this context, "philosophers" refers specifically to the "philosophers of nature" or alchemists who sought the hidden laws of the physical world.</note></term> have hidden. Nevertheless, if he thinks he understands me, yet does not know the nature of the elements and created things, nor the metal of our kingdom, he will labor in vain. But if he understands the volatile and the following natures, he can, through God’s grace, attain it. And I pray to God that he who understands this secret may work for the honor and praise of the highest God.

Know therefore, my dear son, that the ignorant person cannot grasp the secret of this art, because it depends upon the knowledge of the right, true body, which is hidden from him. Understand therefore, my son, the natures: the pure and impure, the clean and unclean, because no thing can give that which it does not itself possess; and nothing acts, nor can it act, except according to its own nature.

Therefore, make use of the most perfect and nearest member. According to the English edition of Mr. <term>Th. Kerckring<note>Theodor Kerckring (1638–1693) was a Dutch physician and alchemist known for his commentaries on the works of Basil Valentine.</note></term>, it reads thus: "use therefore that which is most perfect, and which comes closest to this species, and is also easy to obtain; that will be enough for you." Let the mixed substances go, and take that which is simple and plain (<term>Simplum<note>original: "Simplum"; in alchemy and pharmacy, a "simple" is a basic substance or a single medicinal plant, unmixed with other ingredients.</note></term>), for this is of the <term>Fifth Essence<note>original: "Quinta Essentia"; the most purified and concentrated "quintessence" or life-force of a substance.</note></term>.

Chemical Writings

the fixed <note>original: *fixe*. In alchemy, a "fixed" substance is stable and does not evaporate or change when exposed to heat.</note> remains below and the volatile <note>original: *flüchtige*. In this way, the death and the life of the elements are brought about; when they are joined together, they bloom and grow forth. Thus one thing makes the other perfect and helps it to withstand the fire.

# Of Abbot Synesius

,,alone completes both stones, the White and the Red <note>The "White Stone" was said to transmute base metals into silver, while the "Red Stone" was the final goal, capable of creating gold.</note>. Consider what <term>Geber</term> <note>original: *Geber*. Referring to Jabir ibn Hayyan, a legendary 8th-century figure considered the father of alchemy.</note> says:
That our art does not consist in a multitude of different things, because **Mercury** <note>original: *Mercurius*</note> is a single thing, namely a single stone, in which our mastery consists, to which you add nothing foreign, only that in its preparation you take away all superfluous materials from it, because in this matter all necessary things of the art are contained. # Of Sublimation,
->As the First Work.<-

This is no common, but a Philosophical Sublimation, through which we remove the superfluous parts of that same Stone; this is in truth nothing other than an elevation of the non-fixed part through smoke and vapor, for the fixed part must remain at the bottom. # The Second Work.
## Whitening <note>original: *Dealbatio*; the second major stage of the "Great Work," where the matter is purified and washed of its impurities to reach a silver-like state.</note>.

This process turns our Mercury <term>Mercury: here referring to the "philosophical mercury" or the essential spirit of the matter</term> into a white stone, and this is done solely through the single act of cooking <term>decoction: the process of heating a substance in a liquid to extract its essence or change its state</term>. After the earth has been separated from its water, the vessel should then be placed upon the ashes used in the distillation furnace <note>also called an *athanor*, a furnace designed to maintain a steady, uniform heat over long periods</note>, and the water should be distilled at first with a gentle fire. It must be done so slowly that the water drips at a pace where you could count forty different names or recite fifty-six words between drops <note>In the era before precise clocks, alchemists used the rhythm of speech or counting to measure the rate of distillation and ensure the heat was not too high.</note>.

And this order shall be observed throughout the entire distillation of the black earths; and whatever you find at the bottom, which are the remaining dregs <note>original: *Feces* or *Hefen*; the solid sediment or "lees" left over after distillation</note>, shall then be dissolved with new water. This water should be three or four parts more than the dregs, so that everything may dissolve and be transformed into Mercury and into living quicksilver. I tell you that you must do this as often as necessary until nothing remains but the dregs. 

In this distillation, no specific time is prescribed; rather, it is completed according to whether there is much or little water present, though the intensity of the fire must always be kept in mind. # The Third Work.

## Rubification, or Reddening.
<note>original: *Rubificatio*; this is the final phase of the alchemical Great Work, where the substance reaches its highest power and is colored red, symbolizing the fixed state of the Stone.</note>

Take as much of the white medicine as you wish and place it with its glass vessel upon the hot ashes until it has dried out just as the ashes have. Afterward, give it the Water of the Sun <note>Water of the Sun: likely a reference to gold that has been "dissolved" or a specific solar solvent intended to imbue the substance with the "red" quality of the sun.</note>, which you have specially saved for this work, and continue with the fire at the second degree <note>second degree: a moderate level of heat, often compared to the heat of the sun in midsummer, used to encourage growth without scorching the material.</note>, until it dries out. Then give it more of the aforementioned water again, imbibe and dry it out; thus, one after the other, until the matter becomes red, melts like wax, and flows red upon the metal plate, as has been previously stated; then the matter for the red work will be perfected. 

Note, however, that you must never take more of the Water of the Sun than is just enough to cover the body <note>body: the solid material or "corpus" at the bottom of the vessel.</note>, and no more; this is done so that the Elixir is not submerged and drowned. And thus the fire shall be pursued until it dries out, and then the next <term>imbibition</term> <note>imbibition: from the Latin *imbibitio*, the process of "feeding" or soaking a dry substance with a liquid until it is saturated.</note> shall be undertaken, and thus continued until the medicine is finished—namely, until the action of the <term>digestion</term> <note>digestion: a process of slow, steady heating over a long period, mimicking the natural maturation of minerals in the earth.</note> of the fire has turned it into a red powder, which is the true Oil of the Philosophers, the bloody stone, the purple-colored red coral, the precious ruby, the red Mercury, and the red Tincture.

# Projection,
## or Throwing-on.
<note>original: *Aufwerffung*; the final stage of alchemy where the Philosopher's Stone is "thrown" onto molten base metal to transform it into gold or silver.</note>

The more you dissolve and coagulate again, the more the power is infinitely increased. Note, however, that the Medicine increases more slowly through dissolution than through <term>fermentation</term> <note>fermentation: in alchemy, this is the process of joining the "Stone" with pure gold or silver to "ripen" it and give it a specific direction or "flavor."</note>. Therefore, that which is dissolved does not well accomplish its effect if it is not previously <term>fixed</term> <note>fixed: *figirt*; to make a substance "fixed" means to make it resistant to the heat of the fire so that it no longer evaporates or flies away.</note> in its ferment; nevertheless, the <term>multiplication</term> <note>multiplication: the process of increasing the potency and quantity of the alchemical medicine so that one part can transform thousands of parts of base metal.</note> of the dissolved Medicine is more abundant, or richer and more superfluous, than that which is fermented, because the subtlety there is greater. I tell you here for your information that in the multiplication you must throw one part of the work over four parts of the other, thus it will become powder in less time, according to the nature of the ferment.

# Way to Truth.

Now that, dear friend and brother, many deceptions have been presented until now to the simple-minded in the glorious art of **Chemistry** <note>original: "Chymia." # The Only
## Way to Truth.

Now, dear friend and brother, many deceptions have until now been presented to the simple-minded <note>In this context, the "simple-minded" refers to the uninitiated or gullible seekers who lack proper chemical training.</note> in the magnificent art of Chemistry <note>original: "Chymia."</note> by many false alchemical writers <note>original: "Scribenten."</note>. They proceed with the [laboratory] work, but thereby bring themselves into great toil and labor; for what is begun out of ignorance cannot be brought to a praiseworthy end.

They believe they have found the right, true art there—which, however, is never described in books without parables <note>Metaphorical stories or allegories used to hide chemical secrets from the unworthy.</note>. From this simple <note>The original German "schlechte" here means "plain" or "simple" rather than "bad."</note> cooking and graduation, the subtle <term>sophists|Deceptive practitioners who used complex language to hide their lack of practical success or to intentionally mislead others.</term> have invented <term>dissolution</term>, <term>coagulation</term>, <term>calcination</term>, <term>putrefaction</term>, <term>sublimation</term> <note>These are the traditional "Twelve Gates" or stages of alchemy, which the author argues are merely different aspects of one single process.</note>, and many more fanciful names besides. They have falsely invented these things out of hatred and envy so that they might lead followers away from the true Art and into great poverty, for which they will find it difficult to answer before **God**, considering little what **God** says:

They have trampled the truth underfoot and put lies in its place, which they have grandly adorned and written great books about, as if it were a weighty matter to improve the metallic nature, when it is actually nothing else than a simple cooking. # Toward Truth

...and even trample underfoot that in which you are so deeply rooted, and you think no differently than that you know some great thing, which is nonetheless nothing but a great folly and a fool’s game. This serves not for the improvement of the **metallic natures** <term>metallic natures|original: Metallischen Naturen; the inner essence or "soul" of metals that alchemists sought to refine</term>, but serves only the barbers and bath-house keepers, and also the **physicians** <term>physicians|original: Medicis</term>; so let them play with it, for it is occasionally of use to them.

Just as also **Adam von Bodenstein** <note>A 16th-century Swiss physician and alchemist who was a major proponent of Paracelsus's work, though criticized here as a "sophist."</note>, who was a master in **sophistry** <term>sophistry|original: Sophisterey; in alchemy, this refers to false or superficial chemical practices that do not lead to the true Philosopher's Stone</term>, wherefore he published many strange books under the guise of **Theology** <note>original: "The." abbreviation for Theologie</note> and boasted greatly of himself through **alchemy** <term>alchemy|original: Alchymi</term>, as if he truly knew it—which is far from the truth. A good sophist, I confess, he was; for all his doing is nothing but dealing with sophistical regimes, through which he discovered several **preparations** <term>preparations|original: Praeparationes; chemical mixtures or medicines</term> (by the power of the **common fire** <note>External, physical heat, as opposed to the internal "secret fire" of the alchemists.</note>) which were useful to him in his trade, such as in **medicine** <term>medicine|original: Medicin</term>. This, however, does not pertain to true alchemy, but is indeed contrary to it. Nevertheless, there are many people today who attribute true alchemy to **Bodenstein** and think he understood all the secrets well, though he missed the mark widely. To the unlearned, it appears confusing to the eyes, as if a mighty understanding were within it; yet it is an unfounded thing to the wise. However, as the saying goes, it is easy to fence for the blind <note>A proverb meaning it is easy to deceive those who lack the knowledge to see the truth.</note>, so I will let it rest at that, since **Adam von Bodenstein** does not [present] his person...

# The Only Way

...present, I do not wish to slander him much, according to the proverb: **Of the absent, say nothing but good** <note>original Latin: *De absentibus nil nisi bonum*</note>. But this I say: he was a physician and a good **sophist** <term>sophist|original: Sophist; in an alchemical context, this refers to someone who uses deceptive, overly complex, or purely theoretical methods rather than following the true laws of nature</term>, but the natural art of **alchemy** <term>alchemy|original: Alchymey</term>, or the **secrets of nature** <note>original: *Secreta* of the natures</note>, he did not truly understand, as evidenced by his own writings. Although it does not concern me much to highly praise anyone—and they will do me no harm by it—it harms the poor, plain, and simple people who rely on them and are thereby led into ruin. It is for their sake that I write this, so that they may know what they should guard against; for the deception is great, but the **truth is simple** <note>original: *Warheit ist schlecht*; in Early Modern German, "schlecht" often meant "straightforward," "plain," or "simple" rather than "bad."</note>.

If truth now pleases you, you must abandon **sophistry** <term>sophistry|original: Sophisterey</term> with all its labor that you have practiced until this day, and only observe what nature does, and how she **works toward the essence** <note>original: *ad Essentiam laboriret*</note>. In this way you will not fail nor err, but you will sow what you desire and have no trouble; you will also require little labor or spending of money.

For with a subtle and slight **cooking** <term>cooking|original: Kochung; the application of gentle, steady heat to a substance over a long period, akin to digestion</term>, the whole matter is accomplished, so that through the cooking occurs the **dissolving and thickening of bodies** <note>original: *Solutio* and *Coagulatio Corporum*</note>, and the **sublimation** <term>sublimation|original: Sublimation; the process of heating a substance until it becomes a vapor and then solidifies again, used to purify materials</term> along with the **putrefaction** <term>putrefaction|original: Putrefaction; a stage of "decay" where the matter turns black, seen as a necessary death before chemical rebirth</term> are all finished thereby, about which the wise have also written. But yet, several have set up an entirely different essence instead of the true, simple essence, whereby the whole world is blinded and many a person led into great harm.

# Toward the Truth

Whether it was done rightly, I leave to God, who will judge all things; for it would be much better if so much were not written, whereby many a person is troubled, who rely solely on the **sophistical, invented processes** <term>sophistical processes|original: Sophistische erdichtete Process; refers to overly complicated, unnatural laboratory procedures created through human intellect rather than following nature’s simple laws</term> which they learn in these **books of lies** <note>The author frequently attacks standard alchemical texts as deceptive or intentionally confusing.</note> and are thus deceived. If there were not so much written about **alchemy** <term>alchemy|original: Alchymi</term>, or if it were not daily written about by those who do not understand nature, there would be many thousands of people today who would have known the true art and would have been able to grasp it for themselves. 

As it is, in many years hardly one can arrive at the **truth** <note>original: *Warheit*</note>, because almost all lovers of **philosophy** <term>philosophy|original: Philosophey; in this context, the theoretical study of nature’s hidden powers</term> rely solely on the books and sophistical work, thinking that the ancients also achieved it with such great labor. I publicly rebuke this and say that it is not so; for the true art requires no part of the **bungling** <term>bungling|original: Hümplerey; refers to clumsy, unscientific, or trial-and-error work in the laboratory</term> used by the **laborers** <term>laborers|original: Laboranten; specifically those who perform repetitive chemical operations without true insight into nature</term> of today. 

The ancient sages themselves did not work in such a manner, even if they taught somewhat more extensively in their books to blind the unwise; in this, they did not do well, for even those who might have been on the right path could be led into error, unless they were taught otherwise by **living teachers** <note>original Latin: *vivos Præceptores*</note>.

But since limits are also prescribed and goals set for the living masters as to how far and to whom they may **reveal** <note>The catchword *ren* completes the word *offenbaren* (to reveal) which would begin the next page.</note> such secret art—

# The Only Way

...[reveal] should or may, so that they are not found to be violators of the seal of **Divine Mystery** <term>Divine Mystery|original: Göttlicher Geheimnuß; the sacred secrets of creation that God has hidden within the natural world</term> and subject to the curse of all **philosophers** <term>philosophers|original: Philosophorum; here referring to the "true" alchemists of antiquity</term>, it is better—setting aside all books and human teachers—to look at **Nature** alone. One should observe her wonderful operation not only in the production of **metals** but also in all things that grow from the earth. Consider her **circulation** <term>circulation|original: Circulation; the rhythmic, cyclical movement of moisture and energy through the earth and atmosphere</term> in winter and summer, in spring and autumn—yes, day and night. Keep heat and warmth always before your eyes and reflect upon them. For when you are thoroughly aware of from what and how **Nature** brings each thing into its growth, bloom, fruit, and perfection, it will henceforth not be difficult for you to apply your hands in a manner according to Nature. From the **Matter** <term>Matter|original: Materia; the fundamental substance or "prime matter" used by Nature to form all things</term> which Nature uses in the caves of the earth for various growths, you too can put your intention into practice and complete it according to your desire.

Therefore I ask you, dear brother, that you would not take it ill of me, but rather interpret it for the best, that I so completely reject and despise your previous work which you have done and still do daily in **alchemy** <term>alchemy|original: Alchymi</term>. I truly do this for your own good, because I know that no person in the whole world who is engaged in such work (as you are) will ever achieve anything good, or reach the true trans- <note>The page ends mid-word; the catchword "lung" indicates the word is "Verwandlung" (transformation/transmutation).</note>

# Toward the Truth

...[transform]ation of metals, toward which you strive, could ever come to pass.

Therefore, I tell you once more, and in abundance, that you must abandon such labor and give me your ear; for I write to you the true **Truth** <note>original: "wahre Warheit"; a redundant emphasis common in Baroque writing to stress absolute sincerity and divine inspiration</note>, for which I desire to be held accountable before **GOD**. I have no need to fill the world with more lies, for it has already been filled more than enough by ignorant people who were themselves blind to the natural workings of **Nature**. These people allowed themselves to be seduced by false books and devoted themselves to **sophistical** <term>sophistical|original: Sophistiſche; in an alchemical context, this refers to "false" or "deceptive" alchemy that uses chemical tricks rather than following natural laws</term> works, thereby squandering their house and home. They were unable to accomplish anything useful for the true **Art** <term>Art|original: Kunst; the "Great Work" (Magnum Opus) of alchemy, specifically the creation of the Philosopher's Stone</term>, remaining stuck therein as if in a labyrinth, and completely despaired of the truth of the Art.

These same people later continued and began to write as if they understood the matter well or had gained great advantage from it; thus they became poor **bunglers** <note>original: "Stümplern"; unskilled amateurs or dabblers who lack true philosophical understanding</note>.

For they have **dissolved** <term>dissolved|original: ſolvirer (from Latin solvere); the process of breaking a solid down into liquid, often using harsh acids</term> for so long that all their money and property melted and vanished; they **sublimated** <term>sublimated|original: ſublimiret; heating a substance to turn it into vapor which then cools back into a solid, often a very volatile and dangerous process</term> for so long that their pots and kettles flew out through the chimney; and they **putrefied** <term>putrefied|original: putrificiret; the stage of rot or fermentation meant to "kill" the matter so it can be reborn</term> for so long that the clothes rotted off their bodies. They also **calcined** <term>calcined|original: calciniret; heating a metal or mineral to high temperatures to reduce it to a dry powder</term> for so long that all their wood and coal turned to ash.

# The Only Way

This is now, dear brother, the use and advantage they have obtained through their heavy toil and labor; therefore, let them once more be an example to you, and desist from such **sophistical** <term>sophistical|original: Sophistische; referring to "false" alchemy that focuses on chemical tricks rather than the spiritual and natural laws of the universe</term> labor. For it is not the right way to the true art of **alchemy** <term>alchemy|original: Alchymen</term>, or to the true natural **transformation of metals**, but it is only, as previously said, a way to **sophistry** <term>sophistry|original: Sophisterey</term>, useful for barbers and surgeons <note>original: "Barbieren und Badern"; in this era, barbers and bath-keepers performed minor surgeries, bloodletting, and tooth-pulling, often without formal medical education</note> to prepare their **medicines** <term>medicines|original: Medicamenta</term> through which they may have their profit.

You also perceive how many ignorant people enter into **alchemy**, such as shoemakers, turners, tailors, also ruined, bankrupt merchants and brewers, who with lack of understanding torture themselves for several years in **bungling** <term>bungling|original: Sudley; refers to messy, unrefined, or "kitchen" alchemy practiced by the uninitiated</term>, and find nothing useful for the transformation of metals. Yet they immediately want to be great physicians, making much chatter with boastful, high-flown words, and undertake many great things, even to cure great illnesses, of which they nevertheless have no understanding. They give unknowingly *one thing for another* <note>original: "Quid pro quo"; here meaning the accidental or ignorant substitution of one drug for another</note>, *poisons instead of medicines* <note>original: "Venena pro Medicamentis"</note>, whereby they bring many a person under the earth. For all of this they must answer to **GOD**, who will also—unless they desist—heavily visit <note>original: "heimsuchen"; in this context, it refers to divine punishment or judgment</note> them for it. But enough of this, as the matter does not greatly concern me, for the worldly authorities will surely know how to restrain such boastful, high-flown fellows. But I write to you such—

# The Only Way

In the same way as a child is generated through **coction** <term>coction|original: Kochung; a process of ripening or maturation through steady, natural heat</term> from the **seed** <term>seed|original: Spermata</term> of a man in the mother's womb: and just as a young chick is prepared from the egg through the natural brooding of the hen: so too do the metals have a certain substance from which they are born.

# The Only Way

Things have been divided into three natures / although the three natures are physically distinct, namely *vegetable*, *animal*, and *mineral*, they are nonetheless elemental or, in secret, sprouted from a single substance; they all have one single root from which they all flourish and grow, which the Ancients called a *derivation* <note>original: Verführung; while this modernly means "seduction," in this context it likely refers to the "leading forth" or "induction" of the primary matter</note> of *first matters* <note>original: primarum Materiarum</note>, or *Hyle* <note>original: Hyle; a Greek term used in alchemy to describe primordial, unformed matter</note>, for it is nothing other than the hidden elemental fire with its *liquid* <term>liquid|original: Liquor; a vital fluid or solvent believed to be the life-force of matter</term>, which the Ancients also called *Radical Moisture* <note>original: Radicalem Humorem; in alchemy, the essential fluid believed to sustain the life and form of all substances</note>, in which they spoke rightly, for the *liquid* is a root of all created things.

However, that this moisture along with its fire is divided into distinct natures happens through no other way than alone, as was said, through different cooking <term>cooking|original: Kochung; the natural process of maturation through heat and time within the earth</term> that occurs in Nature; for one nature is cooked more with its elemental fire through its moisture than the other, among which the *vegetable* nature is the least in the cooking, because its *essence* <term>essence|original: Essentia</term> is easily burned and the *liquid* also easily separates from the elemental fire (by the ordinary fire) <note>original: das schlechte Feuer; "schlecht" here means "simple" or "common" fire as opposed to the specialized "elemental fire" of nature.</note>.

The *animal* nature is almost the same as the former in the cooking, for its *essence* also burns easily; therefore the *mineral* nature is the highest in the cooking, because the metallic *liquid* is more and better [refined] through the cooking with the elemental

->towards the Truth.<-

Fire is more unified [in metals] than in the other two natures mentioned previously; for this reason, metals resist common fire better than other things categorized under the vegetable and animal natures. This is plainly visible: when metals are placed in the fire, they do not give off flames like wood, because the wood's *essence* <term>essence|original: Essentia</term> is not cooked with the *liquid* <term>liquid|original: Liquor; the vital moisture or life-force</term> in the same way that metallic moisture is cooked with its *essence*. Furthermore, the union of the *liquid* with the *essence* in wood was not metallic, but merely vegetable, which is consumed in a black smoke. 

However, after the *essence* has undergone the process of cooking through Nature, it has not remained vegetable, but has now become metallic; it is now consumed by common fire in a white smoke, in the same way you see that when imperfect metals <note>Imperfect or "base" metals include lead, tin, copper, and iron, which were believed to be "unripe" versions of gold.</note> are melted in the fire, they give off a white smoke. 

Thus, just as the vegetable *essence* is purified through natural cooking and changed from black smoke into white smoke, for this same reason the ancient Sages said: you must first blacken before you whiten, and thereafter whiten before you make red <note>These refer to the three main stages of the Alchemical Great Work: *Nigredo* (blackening/putrefaction), *Albedo* (whitening/purification), and *Rubedo* (reddening/perfection).</note>. 

This "reddening" is to be understood as making complete and perfect, just as *Sol* <note>original: Sol; Latin for "Sun," the alchemical name for Gold</note> and *Luna* <note>original: Luna; Latin for "Moon," the alchemical name for Silver</note>, those two glorious metals, have become perfect through the cooking, and their essen-

# The Only Way

The **Essence** <term>essence|original: Essentia</term> is completely and utterly united with the **Liquid** <term>liquid|original: Liquor; the vital moisture or life-force of the metal</term>, and together they have become pure fire, which is called "making red" <note>original: roth machen; this refers to *Rubedo*, the final stage of the Alchemical Great Work where the matter reaches perfection.</note> by the Ancients.

Therefore, I say to you, dear friend and brother, do not let yourself be led astray by the old books, which are written so corruptly. Instead, simply learn to recognize the metallic nature thoroughly; in this way, you will easily understand the discourse of the Ancients. You will not wander aimlessly with other alchemists who merely gape at the sayings of the Ancients or convince themselves that one must take a **substance** <term>substance|original: Substantiam</term>, then **purify** and **dissolve** <term>dissolve|original: dissolviren</term> it until the **matter** <term>matter|original: Materia</term> becomes black. They believe they must then wash, **calcine** <term>calcine|original: calciniren; to heat a substance to high temperatures to remove volatile parts or reduce it to powder</term>, and work it until the blackness passes and it begins to become white, and then increase <note>original: augiren; from the Latin *augere*, to increase</note> the fire and calcine or work it until the matter becomes red. All of this is false; it is not a **Philosophical work** <term>philosophical work|original: Philosophische Arbeit; refers to true alchemy that follows the laws of nature</term>, but a truly **Sophistical work** <term>sophistical work|original: Sophistische Arbeit; a term for "false" alchemy that uses chemical shortcuts or literal interpretations of metaphors.</term>.

Thus, all the sayings of the ancient Philosophers are interpreted in a sophistical manner by the ignorant. The Ancients actually quite liked this; indeed, they all spoke so obscurely for that reason, so that no one could rightly interpret or understand what they meant. They certainly all point toward the metals, and they mention **Mercury** <term>mercury|original: Mercurii</term> and **Sulfur** <term>sulfur|original: Sulphur</term> often and at length, but yet it is all for the purpose of deception <note>In alchemical literature, "Mercury" and "Sulfur" often represent philosophical principles rather than the common substances found in a pharmacy.</note>.

<meta>This page continues the transition from the previous discussion on "reddening" (Rubedo) to a direct warning against the common errors of "sophistical" or false alchemists. It elaborates on why trying to extract the metallic essence from finished metals using harsh chemicals or fire is a destructive and futile path.</meta>

->concerning Truth.<-
Cc 3
<meta>catchword: then</meta>

Even though the metallic **essence** <term>essence|original: Essentia; the inner spiritual or medicinal core of a substance</term> is the correct **matter** <term>matter|original: Materia</term> which must be raised through a natural cooking from the lowest to the highest **degree** <term>degree|original: Gradu</term>, those who wrote of it spoke correctly for the wise who understand it rightly. However, for the ignorant, this is a deception because they imagine and guess from the books of the Ancients that it must be taken from the metals, and they then labor and torment themselves with it until it becomes **perfect** <term>perfect|original: perfect</term>. This is **sophistical** <term>sophistical|original: Sophistisch; referring to deceptive, false, or purely chemical alchemy as opposed to the true "Hermetic" path</term> and a wandering on round-about paths, for the metallic essence cannot be extracted from **perfect** <term>perfect|original: perfecten; noble metals like gold and silver</term> metals without harm. The reason is, if one were to try to separate it through fire, the **liquid** <term>liquid|original: Liquor; the vital moisture or life-force of the metal</term> evaporates and the essence is burned along with the earth. Likewise, if one wished to separate the essence of **imperfect** <term>imperfect|original: imperfecten; base metals like lead, tin, or copper</term> metals through "strong waters," **arsenic water** <term>arsenic water|original: Arsenicam</term>, **water of life** <term>water of life|original: Aquam Vitæ; usually refers to distilled alcohol or a potent corrosive solvent</term>, or through lyes, the essence along with its liquid would be **corrupted** <term>corrupted|original: corrumpiret</term> by a foreign moisture that it cannot endure. For the metallic nature desires nothing foreign, nor can it tolerate it; if something foreign mingles with the metallic liquid, it has already strayed from its degree and been snatched away from the metallic nature, establishing a **sophistical order** <term>sophistical order|original: Sophistische Ordnung; an unnatural or artificial arrangement</term>, which you must guard against.

Should you also wish to separate the metallic essence from the perfect metals by any means, that too is just as impossible for you.

<summary>The author warns that extracting the "metallic essence" from existing metals through violent means like fire or acids is a "sophistical" error that destroys the very substance the alchemist seeks. He emphasizes that the metallic nature is easily corrupted by foreign substances, leading the practitioner away from the true path.</summary>
<keywords>metallic essence, sophistical alchemy, corruption of matter, perfect metals, base metals, alchemical solvents, natural cooking</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the argument from the previous section, explaining why perfect metals cannot be easily decomposed. It identifies the "liquid" or "living silver" within metals as the essential spirit that must be united with elemental fire through "natural cooking" (decoction) to reach a state of permanence.</meta>

# The Only Way

For the **liquid** <term>liquid|original: Liquor; the vital moisture or life-force of a substance</term> is perfectly cooked with its elemental fire, and through this cooking has so united itself with the earth that neither fire nor water can separate it.

But if you wished to separate it using **strong water** <note>original: Wasser Fortes; usually referring to Aqua Fortis or nitric acid</note>, the **essence** <term>essence|original: Essentiam; the inner spiritual or medicinal core</term> nevertheless dissolves along with the earth and afterward coagulates again into the same form it was before. No moisture can mingle or unite with the moisture or liquid of **perfect** <term>perfect|original: perfecten; noble metals like gold and silver</term> metals in a way that could corrupt or damage them, as happens to the liquid of **imperfect** metals.

Therefore, it is unnecessary for you to concern or trouble yourself much with this, even though the essence and its liquid are closer to the completion of their cooking in metals than in any other thing.

For this reason, the Ancients said that there is no "living" **sulfur** <term>sulfur|original: Sulphur; the active, masculine, or combustible principle in alchemy</term> in any thing more so than in the metals. Thus, they called the metallic liquid **living silver** <note>original: lebendig Silber; another name for Mercury or the volatile metallic spirit</note>. One should not be distracted by whatever names they give it; it is nonetheless nothing other than the **outstretched eagle** <note>original: ausgespannte Adler; a symbolic term often referring to the volatile spirit or the process of sublimation</note>, or the elemental fire with its elemental liquid, as I have said. This must and shall be united with its fire through a natural cooking until the two are inseparable; for the liquid protects the fire from being consumed, so that they both remain stable and endure even in common fire.

# concerning the Truth.

---

This is what the Ancients have called an **Elixir**, which is as much as to say a **cooked fire**. In this they spoke correctly and gave it the right name; for through the **cooking** <term>cooking|original: Kochung; the alchemical process of decoction, where steady heat is applied to a substance to ripen or mature it</term>, that which was previously raw and uncooked is brought to completion and fully ripened. This fully cooked substance is that which breaks apart and exposes the **imperfect metals** <note>original: imperfecten Metallen; metals such as lead or tin, which alchemists believed were "immature" versions of gold</note>, because they are unable to withstand the fire.

Therefore, do not let yourself grow weary of applying diligence to the cooking, because all the labor that causes so much **botched work** <term>botched work|original: Sudlerey; refers to the messy, unmethodical, and failed experiments of "puffers" or false alchemists</term> for the alchemists is accomplished through this simple cooking alone. Through cooking, the substance purifies itself, raises and **sublimes** <term>sublimes|original: sublimiret; the transition of a substance from solid to vapor and back to solid, used for purification</term> itself, and dissolves itself; all things happen through the cooking.

Consequently, as a way to advise and help you, let all other **putrefaction**, **solution**, **coagulation**, and **calcination** or **sublimation** <note>original: Putrefact. Sol. Coagul. und Calc. oder Subl.; these represent the traditional "gates" or stages of the alchemical Great Work</note> fall away, for they bring no advantage but only harm. Moreover, they lead many men to ruin. You will know well how to guard yourself against this in the future, for I have written this instruction and opinion for you out of a simple and faithful heart. I hope that you will well understand my meaning, and also what you should take up so that you may complete the **Work** <note>original: Werck; the Magnum Opus or the creation of the Philosopher's Stone</note> and follow **Nature** conveniently in the cooking.

<meta>catchword: For</meta>

<summary>The author identifies the Elixir as "cooked fire" and emphasizes that the slow, natural process of decoction (cooking) is the only true way to achieve alchemical transformation, dismissing other complex processes as distractions.</summary>
<keywords>Elixir, cooking, decoction, imperfect metals, botched work, sublimation, the Great Work, alchemy, nature</keywords>

# The Only Way to Truth.

---

Since I have more clearly and openly explained and described to you the right, simple, and truthful Truth, without fables and parables, and I mean well for you, so truly may God help me. <note>original: schlechte; in this context, the word means "simple" or "straightforward," rather than "bad" or "poor."</note>

But nonetheless, you must diligently reflect while reading, and well weigh what I have written to you here. Do not let yourself wonder that I lead you entirely away from the common, wicked path; for you must turn yourself toward another way if you desire to reach the Truth of Nature.

Therefore, you should industriously implore and pray to God the Almighty that He might grant and bestow upon you the true **Philosophical Spirit**, who shall teach you to rightly recognize the **Light of Nature** <term>Light of Nature|original: Licht der Natur; a central concept in Hermetic and Paracelsian philosophy referring to the innate wisdom or divine revelation found within the physical world, guiding the seeker toward hidden truths without the need for traditional academic learning</term>, so that you might arrive at the end for which you so longingly strive.

->come.<-

->**T H E  E N D.**<-
